text: This page describes ADT/ADTLib on upstream/main , and it is the only page of this atlas that documents code no user ever opens. It is here because module behaviour now depends on it: a reader chasing what AREG does with a surface ends up in ADTLib/io/surface.py , not in AREG/ .

ADTLib/__init__.py and io/__init__.py must stay free of imports. They run in the lean Conda environment too, which has neither vtk, nor qt, nor slicer. A single import of one of those at package level would break every submodule import on that route. Submodules that need them import them themselves. package_root() exists for the same reason: it returns the directory that has to be on PYTHONPATH for the Conda side to find the package.

title: Defect confirmed in the code
text: Slicer multiplies <filter-progress> by a hundred, and that factor is written down nowhere. It produced three conventions in one repository: a CLI printing the fraction 0.42 makes 42 appear and the bar advances, the intended use; a CLI printing the integer 2 makes 200 appear, which no bar can represent, so the interfaces compare against 200 to learn that one more patient is done, and the CLI sends it as a pulse 0 → 2 → 0 because Slicer only notifies the widget when the value changes ; and AMASSS, receiving both…

A pytorch3d wheel whose tag does not match the installed torch crashes with undefined symbol on import , not at install time. The tag 0.7.9+pt2110cu128 means torch 2.11.0 and CUDA 12.8; the index is ImageMindAnalytics.github.io/pytorch3d-wheels , because PyPI publishes no wheel for modern combinations and the historical fbaipublicfiles index stopped at Python 3.9 / torch 2.0. torch is installed here too, since computing the tag from whatever torch happens to be present only works if that torch has a wheel at all…

Run under a plain PythonSlicer , the suite reports 188 tests and 4 errors . The four are ModuleNotFoundError: torch in the ALI_CBCT tests, which reach ADTLib/env/cuda.py 's preferred_device() at import time. They are a property of the environment, not of the code: no torch, no device probe.

The code has diverged from the paper on three points: the paper describes a two-pass voxel-based registration (full image then masked image, 10,000 iterations) where the code now runs only one masked pass at 1500 iterations, it reports SimpleElastix where the code uses itk-elastix , and it gets its masks from AMASSS in its UNETR / MONAI version whereas AMASSS is today a nnU-Net v2. Reading the chapter as a description of the module as it currently runs would therefore be a mistake.

title: Unpublished
text: No paper covers AREG_IOSCBCT as implemented here. title: Verification
text: The sheet said so, and the verification confirms it: neither Crossref, nor OpenAlex, nor Europe PMC, nor arXiv, nor HAL, nor NA-MIC project weeks 36 through 43 contain anything about an IOS↔CBCT registration by occlusal landmarks + ICP on an isosurface signed by this group. title: Two code bases
text: Everything numbered below describes the legacy Slicer module (SlicerAutomatedDentalTools at 3c67957, 2026-10-26). The VISOR port, which runs the same tool on a server, is described on its own page, CLIC on VISOR . Callouts below that no longer hold in VISOR say so in their title.

title: Pitfall (legacy only)
text: Legacy (3c67957); not present in VISOR: the VISOR panel is a thin client that sends the scans to a server and runs no conda environment on the workstation (Remote CLICRemote/CLICRemote.py:44,53 ; see CLIC on VISOR ). No WSL path: CondaSetUpCallWsl is never instantiated. On Windows, the argument order of condaRunFilePython expected by the Unix path (used by mistake) is not that of the WSL path: the argument list would go out as the environment name. CLIC is effectively Linux-only.

title: Pitfall (legacy only)
text: Legacy (3c67957); not present in VISOR: the tool reads only .nii and .nii.gz (SADT-VISOR tools/CLIC/src/sadt_clic/pipeline.py:36 ), skips other files, and refuses a request with no NIfTI at all with a readable message ( __init__.py:115-123 ; see CLIC on VISOR ). The widget's selection filter accepts .nrrd , .mha , and .mhd in addition to .nii / .nii.gz , but the runner can only load with nibabel : these three formats pass the filter and fail to load.

title: Pitfall (also true in VISOR)
text: Also true in VISOR: SADT-VISOR tools/CLIC/src/sadt_clic/pipeline.py:136 still calls maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn(weights=None) , see Findings in VISOR . weights_backbone keeps its default ResNet50_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1 even when weights=None : simply building the model triggers a download of the ImageNet weights for ResNet-50. First run offline = failure, before even reaching final_model.pth .

title: Pitfall (also true in VISOR)
text: Also true in VISOR (SADT-VISOR tools/CLIC/src/sadt_clic/pipeline.py:178-182 : the same loop, the same overwrite; see CLIC on VISOR ). Overlap between two instances is settled by overwrite , not by vote: the instance processed last, hence at the lowest score, since torchvision sorts by decreasing score, wins the pixel. And since nothing enforces consistency between neighboring slices, two adjacent slices can classify the same tooth differently.

text: This step 3 plan describes deformable registration by Elastix on the cropped images; the MRI2CBCT page describes, in the current code, no elastix at all: a global registration of two predicted cranial-base surfaces. text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see ALI with VISOR and Using VISOR .

title: Two engines, one window
text: The module picks the right engine on its own based on your data: CBCT for a volume, IOS for an intraoral scan. All you do is say what type your files are and which points you want.

title: "Nothing comes out, or the points look wrong"
text: First check that the models were actually downloaded, then that the data type you checked matches your files. A CBCT processed as an intraoral scan won't produce anything usable.

title: Intraoral scans: teeth need to be identified first
text: On an intraoral scan, the engine aims its measurements tooth by tooth. If your file doesn't have crown identification yet, ALI runs it automatically along the way: expect extra time on the first attempt.

title: DICOM import
text: Use .nii.gz files instead. The module's DICOM path doesn't work in automatic mode.

title: Disk space
text: The temporary folder isn't cleared afterward. On long series, remember to clean it out from time to time.

page: AMASSS: segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: "Small FOV" changes nothing about the computation (legacy module only)
text: The checkbox that switches to a "high definition" list (teeth, root canal, and mandibular canal included) only changes which checkboxes are shown on screen. It does not reduce the field of view or the resolution of the computation: don't expect it to run faster or produce a finer result. The VISOR panel has no such checkbox.

page: AMASSS: segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: Root canal is checked by default, with no model (legacy module only)
text: "Root canal" is checked by default in the structure list, but the published model bundle has no model for it. Checking it produces neither an error nor a segmentation: the failure is silent, the structure is simply missing from the result. With VISOR, "Root canal" is not offered at all.

page: AMASSS: segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: DICOM import (also true with VISOR)
text: The interface offers "DICOM Files" as an input type, but no DICOM conversion actually happens before the computation runs: a DICOM input produces nothing. Use .nii.gz or .nrrd files instead. The VISOR panel offers no DICOM input type either: give it volume files.

page: AMASSS: segmenting structures from a CBCT
title: Don't run two modules at once (legacy module only)
text: AMASSS unconditionally wipes its temporary working folder every time it starts. That same folder is shared with AREG_CBCT and VFACE, which call AMASSS behind the scenes. If you run two of these modules at the same time on the same machine, one can wipe the other's working folder mid-run: let one computation finish before starting another. With VISOR, each run uses its own working folder on the server, so this cannot happen.

title: Which one to pick
text: Already have masks? Semi-Automated. No masks, but T1 scans already oriented the same way? Fully-Automated. Neither? Orientation & Registration. In all three modes, you check one or more reference regions ( Cranial Base , Mandible , Maxilla ): each one runs its own independent registration, with its own output.

title: A patient goes missing, with no error message
text: T1/T2 pairing only works with the _T1 and _T2 suffixes in the file name. Any other convention ( _T3 , _baseline , a date…) keeps AREG_CBCT from recognizing the pair, and that patient is silently dropped: nothing is shown to flag it. If a patient is missing from the output, the first thing to check is that patient's file names.

page: AREG_CBCT: register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: Avoid mask keywords in a scan's file name
text: AREG_CBCT recognizes a mask file by keywords in its name ( seg , mask , pred , or the region's abbreviation: cb , mand , max ). The first file that matches is used as-is, with no check that it's actually a mask. A scan named, say, P1_T1_MAX.nii.gz could therefore be mistaken for a maxilla mask.

page: AREG_CBCT: register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: DICOM import
text: Convert your CBCT scans to .nii.gz before running AREG_CBCT. DICOM input is only offered in Orientation & Registration mode, and stays fragile even there: starting from already-converted files avoids the surprise.

page: AREG_CBCT: register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: The saved matrix can drift slightly from the best alignment found
text: The .tfm file and the registered CBCT stay consistent with each other, but both can drift a bit from the alignment the registration actually found as optimal. The gap depends on where the skull sits in the volume, and stays small when your images are already well centered, which is the case after a run through Orientation & Registration. If you reuse this matrix elsewhere, in AutoMatrix for instance, always check the overlay by eye before trusting it.

page: AREG_CBCT: register a follow-up CBCT onto the baseline
title: "Include Approximation Step" no longer does anything
text: The checkbox stays checked by default in the interface, but it has no effect on the result: don't count on it to speed up or refine a registration that's giving you trouble.

page: AREG_IOS: register two scans of the same patient
title: Legacy module and VISOR
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: AREG_IOS: register two scans of the same patient
title: Two modes, one per arch
text: Butterfly (upper arch): the module predicts the stable palatal patch itself, with a network, and uses it as the registration anchor. MGL (lower arch): there's no palate down there, so the module builds a band along the mucogingival line instead, from landmarks it places automatically.

page: AREG_IOS: register two scans of the same patient
title: No compatible graphics card
text: In Butterfly mode, the palatal patch inference requires a CUDA GPU, full stop. On a machine without a compatible GPU, this mode fails outright. Use MGL on those machines, or process the upper arch elsewhere.

page: AREG_IOS: register two scans of the same patient
title: File naming: order matters
text: Put the arch marker before the timepoint marker in the filename ( P001_Upper_T1.vtk ), not after ( P001_T1_Upper.vtk ): in the wrong order, one of the output matrices won't be found, with no blocking error, the run finishes but an expected file is simply missing. Also avoid the same words (Upper, Lower, U, L, Mx, Md…) in parent folder names: they're read from the full path and can throw off the upper/lower sorting for the whole batch.

page: AREG_IOS: register two scans of the same patient
title: A failed orientation silently breaks the patch
text: If the canonical orientation step can't be computed, for instance because the reference teeth weren't identified, processing doesn't stop: the network still runs, on a badly oriented scan, and nothing flags it. Always check the resulting patch visually before trusting it.

page: AREG_IOS: register two scans of the same patient
title: MGL never produces a transform
text: Whichever regime you pick, auto or semi-auto, MGL mode writes no .tfm file at all. You get the registered surfaces, but not the transform that produced them.

page: AREG_IOS: register two scans of the same patient
title: Output folder and file formats
text: The output folder must already exist: AREG_IOS doesn't create missing subfolders. And your files keep their original extension on write even though the content is always rewritten in VTK format: a .stl or .obj coming out is not a strictly valid STL or OBJ file, so keep it for Slicer rather than handing it to another program.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT: place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: Legacy module and VISOR
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: AREG_IOSCBCT: place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: Three ways to get there
text: Depending on what you already have, nothing, raw scans, or landmarks already placed, the module offers three modes that don't ask for the same input files. See "Three modes" below before you start.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT: place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: No matrix is written
text: Registration produces surfaces that are already transformed, not a matrix file. Unlike AREG_IOS or AREG_CBCT, you cannot reopen the result and nudge it with the mouse: if the alignment is off, the fix is to rerun, with different landmarks or a different setting, not to correct it by hand.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT: place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: One scanned arch means the patient is dropped
text: Every patient must provide both arches, scan and landmarks included. If even one is missing, say, only one arch was ever scanned, the patient disappears from the result with no visible error, only a line in the log. Only when no patient at all can be registered does the run stop with an error.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT: place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: Only T0, T1 and T2 are recognized, and T10 reads as T1
text: The clinical timepoint is read from the file name, and only those three values count. A file marked T3 to T9 matches nothing: the patient is simply left out. A two-digit timepoint is read by its first digit, so T10 to T19 count as T1 and T20 to T29 as T2 , and can be paired with the wrong visit.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT: place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: Check the log when the CBCT surface falls back to 400
text: The surface the scan is registered against is extracted at a level the module reads off each CBCT, half-way between the enamel at the landmarks and the soft tissue around the arch, so it adapts to your scanner and reconstruction. When the crowns are no brighter than what surrounds them, it falls back to a fixed 400 and writes a warning in the log; on such a scan the surface may not follow the teeth, and the registration should be checked by eye.

page: AREG_IOSCBCT: place an intraoral scan into a CBCT's frame
title: The progress bar can announce more patients than it will deliver
text: The interface's counter also recognizes .nrrd , .nii and .gipl for the CBCT. The engine itself only accepts .nii.gz : a patient counted at the start may never actually be processed.

title: Legacy page
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see ASO with VISOR and Using VISOR .

title: Two data types, two ways of working
text: You first tell ASO what kind of files you have: CBCT for a volume, IOS for an intraoral scan. For each, two modes are available. Fully-Automated asks only for your raw scans: ASO places the landmarks it needs itself (via a network, for a CBCT) or segments the teeth (for a scan) before orienting. Semi-Automated skips that prediction step and works directly on landmarks or teeth you have already identified: faster, but it assumes that preparatory work already exists.

title: CBCT semi-automatic: don't run it on its own
text: On a CBCT, the semi-automatic mode needs a transform file that only the automatic mode produces , as part of its recentring step. If you run the semi mode directly on scans that ASO has never processed, it fails patient after patient. In practice, for CBCT, semi-automatic only makes sense as a second pass: for instance to redo the orientation of a series that has already gone through the automatic mode once.

title: Your CBCT landmark files are gone
text: In semi-automatic mode, ASO starts by merging every landmark file it finds in your input folder into a single file, then deletes the originals . Keep a copy of your .mrk.json files elsewhere before running a job, especially if the input folder is also where you keep your only copy of those landmarks.

title: Occlusion: name your files Upper / Lower unambiguously
text: Occlusion mode pairs the upper and lower arches by file name ( Upper / _U_ or Lower / _L_ ). A file whose name carries none of these markers is silently treated as a lower arch: with no error message. Check your file names before turning this option on.

title: Rerunning on a folder that already has output does nothing
text: If an output file already exists under the expected name, ASO does not rewrite it and still reports success. After fixing a setting, point to an empty output folder rather than rerunning on the same one.

page: Agent: let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Legacy module page
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. The VISOR extension ships a copy of this panel that still runs on your computer, and the VISOR server has a separate Agent tool that no panel calls: see Agent with VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: Agent: let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Read this before you try it
text: As the repository stands today, Agent cannot locate the tools it wants to launch . Unless you configure it manually, any attempt to run a tool fails. The mode that only answers, without executing anything, is not affected and works normally.

page: Agent: let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Nothing to install by hand on the Slicer side
text: The required Python packages install themselves automatically on first launch, inside Slicer's own Python.

page: Agent: let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Read every line, carefully
text: For most tools, the mapping between what Agent believes it's passing and what the tool actually expects is off. A run can therefore start with wrong values without any error warning you beforehand: the confirmation dialog is your only real check.

page: Agent: let a local assistant pick the tool
title: "Nothing launches, or the error makes no sense"
text: As the repository stands, Agent can't find the scripts it wants to run on its own: unless you tell it yourself where they are, execution fails before it even starts. The automatic repair step that follows can't fix this: the problem isn't in the parameters, it's in the script's path.

page: Agent: let a local assistant pick the tool
title: A run starting with wrong values
text: See above: always check the confirmation dialog before approving. A parameter mismatch usually shows up only by eye, in that dialog, not in an error message.

page: Agent: let a local assistant pick the tool
title: Everything is slow without a graphics card
text: If the model server is running without a GPU, expect each reply to take roughly a minute and a half . A back-and-forth conversation adds up to minutes, not seconds.

page: AutoCrop3D: crop a series of volumes
title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: AutoCrop3D: crop a series of volumes
title: The ROI must be an axis-aligned box, saved as-is
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Not quite the same with VISOR. The server reads the coordinate system, so a ROI saved in RAS is converted. A genuinely rotated box is still cropped as its axis-aligned self, but the run report now says so ( roi_orientation_ignored ). The "see below" option for tilted images does not exist there. Details: With VISOR . The fast crop path completely ignores the orientation and coordinate system declared in the ROI file: it only reads the center and size, and assumes a box aligned with the…

page: AutoCrop3D: crop a series of volumes
title: A folder with exactly one ROI file → error
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Not the case with VISOR : a folder holding exactly one ROI is applied to every scan. If you're using per-patient ROIs but the folder holds only a single .mrk.json file, the module errors out instead of applying it to every volume. In that case, point it directly at that file as a single shared ROI rather than at the folder containing it.

page: AutoCrop3D: crop a series of volumes
title: Per-patient ROI: matching breaks on an underscore
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Not the case with VISOR : scans and ROIs go through one naming rule, so Patient_01_Scan.nii.gz and Patient_01_ROI.mrk.json pair. A scan without a ROI is named in the panel's status line (up to five names) and in the report, and a run that crops nothing fails with a message instead of ending with an empty folder. Volume names and ROI names aren't split the same way when they're compared. Patient IDs without an underscore ( MA0001_Scan.nii.gz / MA0001_ROI.mrk.json ) match fine; an…

page: AutoCrop3D: crop a series of volumes
title: The interface rejects formats the crop itself accepts
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Not the case with VISOR : the panel is generated from the server's description and a folder of plain .nii , .nrrd or .gipl files is accepted. The one exception is .nrrd.gz , which is refused file by file with a message (a gzipped NRRD has no ITK reader). The interface's input check only recognizes compressed volumes ( .nii.gz , .nrrd.gz , .gipl.gz ). A folder of uncompressed .nii or .nrrd files gets rejected ("Wrong type of patient file detected") even though the crop itself handles them…

page: AutoCrop3D: crop a series of volumes
title: "Use module Crop Volume for tilted images": read first
text: Legacy only. The VISOR panel has no such checkbox: that engine needs a running Slicer and was not ported. This is the only way to handle a genuinely rotated ROI, but it changes two things. First, it resamples the volume into the ROI's own frame: voxel values get modified, so the "no resampling, registration matrix still valid" benefit no longer applies. Second, it clears the entire Slicer scene for every patient it processes: don't use it if you have data loaded that you want to keep.

page: AutoCrop3D: crop a series of volumes
title: Generating a VTK mesh from a segmentation
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Different with VISOR : there is an explicit Surfaces option ( segmentations by default, or all , or none ). With the default, only files whose name contains a whole word among seg , segmentation , mask , pred , label , labels get a mesh, the folder name does not count, the mesh is placed in the scan's own space and each structure keeps its own colour. Triggers automatically whenever "seg" appears anywhere in the output path (a Segmentations/ folder, for instance). Treat it as a secondary…

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: One matrix, one motion
text: Also true with VISOR . The server moves landmark points through the inverse of the transform, so a scan and its landmarks keep the same relative motion. Applied to a volume, the matrix moves its content. Applied to a landmark file, it moves the points by exactly the same motion. That's what keeps a scan and its landmarks aligned after going through AutoMatrix: as long as you use the same matrix for both.

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: The mirror isn't centered on your patient
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Different with VISOR. The mirror matrix is the server's hosted file, applied through the box Use the mirror matrix . The panel does not offer a reference volume, and without one the VISOR output grid follows the transform; for a reflection about the world origin this can leave the result empty. See With VISOR . The reflection happens across the sagittal plane of the scene's origin, not the patient's own sagittal plane. If your patient isn't already centered in the scene, the result will…

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: Some advertised formats no longer work
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Partly changed with VISOR . The VISOR panel no longer offers meshes or .npy matrices, and nothing counts them. A .txt file holding a plain 4x4 matrix is accepted there. The interface still offers meshes ( .vtk , .vtp , .stl , .off , .obj ) as input scans for intraoral surfaces, and matrices as .npy , both get counted in the progress bar, but neither produces any output: each file of that kind is simply skipped, with a line in the error log. A .txt matrix only works if it's an actual ITK…

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: A failed match gives no warning
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Different with VISOR. Files and transforms left unpaired are named in AutoMatrix_report.json ( without_a_transform , transforms_without_a_file ), and a run that writes nothing stops with an error. The status line in Slicer does not show them, see With VISOR . If a scan's name and a matrix's name don't reduce to the same patient identifier (see above), that file is simply never transformed: no error message, no visible warning. If a patient is missing from the output, the first thing to…

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: One output can overwrite another
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Not the case with VISOR : when a patient has several transforms, each output gets its transform's name whatever the option says. If you uncheck the option that appends the matrix name to the output file, and a patient has more than one matrix, every result gets the same file name: each one overwrites the last, and only the final matrix processed survives. Keep this option checked whenever you're applying more than one matrix per patient.

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: A landmark file can vanish silently
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Partly changed with VISOR . The failure is written under that patient in the report instead of a log line, and the patient's volume is still produced, so scan and landmarks can still disagree. Check the report. Some transformations (dense deformation fields, B-splines) can't be inverted mathematically. When that happens, the matching landmark file is skipped with just a warning in the log, while the volume itself still gets transformed, so a scan and its landmarks can end up out of sync…

page: AutoMatrix: apply a matrix across a whole batch of files
title: Matrices aren't chained
text: Also true with VISOR . Each transform is applied to the original file. When a patient has several matrices, each one is applied separately to the original input file: you get one output file per matrix, never a composition of one after the other.

page: BatchDentalSeg: segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: Legacy module on this page
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: BatchDentalSeg: segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: One extension to install first (legacy module only)
text: BatchDentalSeg relies on the external Slicer extension NNUnet to run the computation. It doesn't install itself: get it through the Extensions Manager, then restart Slicer. Without it, the module shows a message and refuses to start. With VISOR, nothing is installed in Slicer: the NNUnet extension is not needed.

page: BatchDentalSeg: segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: NasoMaxillaDentSeg: don't trust the displayed names or colors (legacy module only)
text: On this model, the label and color shown on screen for four of the six segments don't match the real structure: for instance, what's displayed as "Upper Teeth" is actually the maxilla. This isn't just a display glitch: the value written into the exported file follows the wrong name too, and the mandibular canal segment can be dropped entirely from the export when no match is found. If you use this model, check each segment individually before trusting its name. With VISOR, no segment is renamed: the six values…

page: BatchDentalSeg: segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: UniversalLabDentalsegmentator does not segment the skull
text: Its description in the interface, and the upstream model's own documentation, suggests it includes the skull. It doesn't: its 55 structures are teeth, mandible, maxilla, and the mandibular canal, with no "skull" structure at all. Don't reach for this model expecting a cranial segmentation.

page: BatchDentalSeg: segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: Switching models later can wipe the others' weights (legacy module only)
text: Re-downloading or updating DentalSegmentator's weights clears the entire models folder, including anything already downloaded for PediatricDentalsegmentator, NasoMaxillaDentSeg, and UniversalLabDentalsegmentator. If you switch between models, expect to re-download them. With VISOR, models are staged on the server and nothing is downloaded when you run.

page: BatchDentalSeg: segment CT/CBCT scans in bulk
title: Your files aren't being picked up (legacy module only)
text: Only .nii , .nii.gz , .gipl , and .gipl.gz are recognized, and only at the top level of the chosen folder: a scan in NRRD or sitting in a subfolder is silently ignored. Two different folders containing a scan with the same base name will overwrite the same output: give your files unique names. With VISOR, NRRD files and subfolders are read, and the output keeps your folder tree, so same-named scans in different folders no longer collide.

page: CLIC: find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see CLIC with VISOR and, for the general workflow, Using VISOR .

page: CLIC: find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: The progress bar doesn't move: that's expected
text: While the tool runs, the progress bar stays at zero and nothing shows up in the Slicer scene, even after processing has finished. This is not a crash: the result file is written to disk in the output folder regardless. You have to go find it and load it yourself : see below where it lands.

page: CLIC: find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Accepted formats that don't actually work
text: The file picker also lists .nrrd , .mha , and .mhd . Don't use them: processing can only read .nii / .nii.gz , and fails on the other formats regardless of what the picker allowed.

page: CLIC: find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Linux only
text: The module has no working path on Windows, whatever the README says. Run it on a Linux Slicer installation.

page: CLIC: find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Cancel does nothing
text: It stops neither the running computation nor the underlying process. If you genuinely need to stop, close Slicer.

page: CLIC: find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: The first run needs internet access
text: Building the network downloads generic pretrained weights before the trained model is applied on top. Without a connection on the first attempt, processing fails.

page: CLIC: find and classify impacted canines on a CBCT
title: Two model files in the folder
text: With more than one model file in the models folder, whichever name sorts first alphabetically gets used, with no warning. Keep a single .pth file in that folder to avoid any ambiguity.

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see CNE with VISOR and, for the general workflow, Using VISOR . Note that with a VISOR server your notes are sent to that server.

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: Nothing leaves your machine (legacy module only)
text: This holds for the legacy Slicer module only, not for VISOR. In the legacy module the model runs inside Slicer's own Python, on your computer. Notes aren't sent to any online service during extraction: the only step that touches the network is the one-time model download. With a VISOR server, the text of your notes is uploaded to that server: see CNE with VISOR .

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: The Dashboard is built for TMJ notes
text: It looks for the fields the TMJ model writes (headache, jaw clicking, disc displacement, maximum opening...). Extractions made in Ortho mode list orthodontic findings instead (wire size, elastics, overjet...), so they would most likely stop the Dashboard with an error saying the keys do not match. That is deduced from the lists of fields in the code and on the model cards, not tested on Ortho output.

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: Notes sorted into per-patient subfolders
text: CNE only looks at files sitting directly in the folder you chose, not at anything inside subfolders. A folder organized with one subfolder per patient will produce no output at all, with no error message.

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: Scanned PDF
text: PDF text extraction doesn't do OCR: if your PDF is actually a scanned image, the extracted text is empty and the note can't produce anything.

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: Tables inside a .docx
text: Only paragraph text is read from a Word document; table content is skipped. If your key information sits in a table, it never reaches the model.

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: Note too long
text: There's no chunking: a note longer than the model can read in one pass fails entirely instead of being processed in pieces. The margin is especially tight in Ortho mode.

page: CNE: extract information from clinical notes
title: No anonymization
text: Notes are read as-is, with no personal-data removal. If your files contain identifying information, run them through MedicalDataAnonymizer first if needed.

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see DOCShapeAXI with VISOR and, for the general workflow, Using VISOR .

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Three shape families, one window
text: The data type you pick is the only thing that decides which model runs and which categories come out: Mandibular Condyle : a severity stage out of 4 classes . Nasopharynx Airway Obstruction , three results produced one after another in a single run: presence or absence of obstruction ( 2 classes ), a severity stage ( 4 classes ), and a continuous ratio of obstruction between 0 and 100. Alveolar Bone Defect in Cleft : a severity stage out of 4 classes . For all three severity stages, the 4 classes are really…

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: The map only shows part of what mattered
text: The model decides by combining two sources: the shape of a sampled point cloud and a rendering of several views of the mesh. The explainability map only describes the second one. If a decision leaned mostly on the point-cloud geometry, the map you see will look faint: with nothing to tell you that's the reason, rather than the decision genuinely having no clear focus.

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Two runs, not necessarily the same result
text: The points sampled from the mesh are not drawn the same way twice. Two passes on the same files can therefore produce slightly different saliency maps, and in cases sitting near the boundary between two classes, a different predicted class.

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: The output folder has to exist before you launch
text: If the folder you point to doesn't exist yet, the model download is simply skipped, and the error only surfaces later, when the model tries to load. Create the output folder yourself before starting.

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Adding files mid-way has no effect
text: The list of meshes to process is only rebuilt if it doesn't already exist in the output folder. If you drop more meshes into the input folder without changing the output folder, they simply won't be processed.

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Disk space
text: The downloaded model isn't cached: every new output folder re-downloads it in full. Across several batches, reuse the same output folder where you can, or clean up the old ones.

page: DOCShapeAXI: classify a 3D shape and see what drove it
title: Re-running on the same folder
text: Prediction columns are overwritten in place on every re-run, but columns left over from a different task are never cleared out: they sit side by side in the csv.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Legacy module on this page
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR . The VISOR version does not offer the free-hand outline, the automatic lower-arch band or the automatic crown segmentation.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Two ways to build the stable area
text: On an upper arch, the area is anchored on the palate: pick four reference teeth and FlexReg builds a butterfly-shaped patch around them, or draw its outline directly with the mouse. On a lower arch, with no palate to act as a stable plate, FlexReg instead relies on the mucogingival line, placed automatically, then thickens it into a band running along the gum.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: A graphics card is mandatory (with VISOR: on the server)
text: Building the patch and running the registration only work with a compatible GPU. Without one, these steps fail outright: this isn't a performance nicety, it's a hard requirement of the module. With VISOR, the card is the server's, and only the patch step uses it: your computer needs none.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: "The registration only looks at the teeth I checked"
text: FlexReg aligns only the area you marked out: never the whole arch. If the result looks off away from that area, that's expected: the rest of the mesh simply follows the motion computed on the patch, it isn't registered independently.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Mucogingival landmarks can be unreliable (legacy module only)
text: On the lower arch, some automatically placed points can be markedly less trusted than the others (the measured error jumps from roughly 1 mm to over 4 mm in those cases). FlexReg drops them by default and bridges the gap by interpolation, so a point can look "missing" even though it was detected. VISOR does not place these landmarks at all.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: DICOM import (also true with VISOR)
text: Start from already-exported .vtk or .stl files. The registration itself doesn't read DICOM.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Input file gets overwritten (legacy module only)
text: Drawing the stable area and running crown segmentation both rewrite the input file, not a copy. Always keep a backup of your original scans before you start. With VISOR, your input is never modified: results are written to the output folder with a suffix.

page: FlexReg: register two scans by drawing the stable area yourself
title: Steeply tilted arch: the patch can overshoot
text: The butterfly patch's outline is decided by flattening the arch into a projection. On a strongly tilted arch, that projection can pick up points that are actually far away in height, producing a patch that spills past the intended area: check the preview before committing.

page: GreedyReg: register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: GreedyReg: register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: Three modes, one real registration
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Different with VISOR. The server tool has a single mode, the equivalent of Automatic Registration on two folders. Manual Alignment and Distant Registration do not exist there. Details: With VISOR . Only Automatic Registration actually performs an intensity-based registration. Manual Alignment and Distant Registration only prepare a starting point, to be refined afterward.

page: GreedyReg: register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: "Save Registered Volume" does nothing in Distant mode
text: Legacy only. There is no Distant mode and no "Save Registered Volume" button with VISOR . This mode does not produce a registered volume, only a starting matrix: the button always answers "No result to save!". Use "Save Transform Matrix" instead, or go straight to Automatic Registration to get a volume worth saving.

page: GreedyReg: register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: Misleading checkboxes in Distant mode
text: Legacy only. There is no Distant mode with VISOR . Checking several structures (cranial base, mandible, maxilla) does not combine them. Only one region is actually used, chosen by a fixed priority order (cranial base first, then mandible, then maxilla), regardless of which boxes you checked.

page: GreedyReg: register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: In batch, one failure stops everything, not always clearly
text: Legacy module (3c67957). Not the case with VISOR : a patient that fails is recorded in the report and the others go on. The run stops with an error only when no pair could be registered. The remark about Distant mode does not apply. On a full folder, the first case that fails halts the entire run: no resume, no list of the remaining cases. In Distant mode, a failed landmark prediction does not always surface as an obvious error: the only visible sign can be a quiet "only 0 matched landmarks" in the log.

page: GreedyReg: register two CBCT scans with the ITK-SNAP engine
title: Temporary folders are never cleaned up
text: Legacy only. With VISOR , the server removes its working folder for each patient. Whether after an automatic registration or a manual session, the module does not clear its working folders. On a long series, disk usage builds up; clean them yourself from time to time, but only after saving your results, since that is also where "Save Registered Volume" pulls its file from in Automatic mode.

page: MRI2CBCT: align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: Legacy module page
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. It is not available through a VISOR server: see MRI2CBCT and VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: MRI2CBCT: align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: What it registers
text: The module does not match the two images' brightness. It asks a network to find the cranial base on the CBCT and another to find it on the MRI, then fits the two surfaces together. So the result is only as good as those two outlines, which is why it can pause to let you check them.

page: MRI2CBCT: align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: Restart after the first setup
text: If PyTorch had to be installed or replaced for your graphics card, the panel asks you to restart Slicer and press Run again. On Linux, the registration library needs a system with glibc 2.31 or newer.

page: MRI2CBCT: align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: A patient is skipped
text: A file with no ID at the start of its name, an MRI without a CBCT (or the reverse), or a patient with more than one CBCT is left out, and the panel lists them before it starts. Keep your output folder outside the MRI and CBCT folders: the folders are read recursively, so an earlier run's results could be picked up as new scans.

page: MRI2CBCT: align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: Read the verdict, not only the file name
text: A joint can come out FLAG (weak overlap) and still be saved under a normal file name; only summary.csv and the message at the end say so. SMALL means the MRI outline was very small, the case that most often fails. Anything tagged _FLAGGED , FLIP or _MIRRORED deserves a look before you rely on it.

page: MRI2CBCT: align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: Wrong side
text: The side of a single-joint MRI comes from its position in the file. If it is wrong, swap it at the first pause. If you did not pause, the module can still recover by trying the other side, but only when the first answer was a flip.

page: MRI2CBCT: align an MRI and a CBCT of the TMJ
title: The log disappears
text: The run log lives with the intermediate files, which are deleted after a successful run unless you tick "Keep the intermediate files".

page: MedX: summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: Legacy module page
text: This page describes the module as it was before it was removed from the legacy extension on 2026-09-17; it is no longer in the current version. It was never available through a VISOR server: see MedX and VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: MedX: summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: Two independent paths
text: MedX has two tabs, two buttons, and nothing chains them together automatically. Summarize reads your documents and writes one summary file per patient. Dashboard reads those summaries back and produces the figure page. Once summarization finishes, it's on you to switch tabs and launch the dashboard yourself: it doesn't start on its own.

page: MedX: summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: The model download button does nothing
text: Clicking the download button creates the expected folder but never puts a file in it: the field stays empty and a warning message appears. Get the model archive yourself from the GitHub releases page of the SlicerAutomatedDentalTools repository (the BART.zip file, under the "MedX" release), unzip it, then point the module at that folder.

page: MedX: summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: The dashboard progress bar never moves
text: Unlike the Summarize path, the Dashboard progress bar stays still for the whole run. That isn't a sign it's stuck: let it run and wait for dashboard.png to show up in the output folder.

page: MedX: summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: An empty input folder crashes the module
text: Running either path on a folder with no usable document raises an error instead of a clean message. Check that the folder you picked actually has files in it before you launch.

page: MedX: summarize reports, then build a dashboard
title: Two runs, two different summaries
text: The model isn't deterministic: running the Summarize path again on the exact same documents won't reproduce the previous summary word for word. If you need to compare results over time, keep the _summary.txt files you already have rather than regenerating them.

title: Legacy module page
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. The VISOR extension ships a copy of it that runs on your computer, never on the server, and it does not de-identify the files other panels upload: see MedicalDataAnonymizer with VISOR and Using VISOR .

title: This does not anonymise images
text: Despite the name, no DICOM tag is touched, not the patient's name, birth date, study identifier, or institution, and no face is removed from a CBCT or scanner volume. If images are what you need de-identified, this tool does nothing for you: you need a dedicated DICOM anonymiser, plus separate defacing if the volumes cover the face.

title: A failure can look like a success
text: If processing a document fails, for any reason, the output file comes out with the original text untouched , and the interface still reports "Complete!" No counter, no report, no visible warning marks the difference: a document that was never anonymised is indistinguishable from a clean one until you open it yourself. Reopen and read through every output file before handing it off or publishing it.

title: Dependency installation fails
text: It needs internet access to download Presidio and the language model. If installation errors out, check the connection and try again; Slicer will need restarting once it succeeds either way.

title: Two files with the same name, only one comes out
text: The output folder is written flat: the input's subfolder structure isn't reproduced, and if two subfolders each hold a file with the same name, the second one silently overwrites the first. Rename ahead of time if that's a risk.

title: A .csv comes out unreadable
text: It's the most fragile format here: columns aren't preserved as-is. For tabular data you need to keep usable, anonymise a separate text copy and rebuild the table by hand.

title: The interface looks frozen
text: That's expected: processing runs on Slicer's main thread. On a large folder, leave it running and don't close Slicer, even though nothing else responds in the meantime.

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: A spreadsheet-only tool
text: SurgMovPred doesn't read any volume, surface, or Slicer landmark, and it doesn't touch your 3D scene: nothing is created or displayed there. Everything happens on disk: a folder of spreadsheets in, a folder of spreadsheets out.

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: Each point is predicted on its own, not the whole segment
text: The 112 output values come from 112 independent models, one per value. Nothing guarantees that the ten points predicted for the maxilla, say, stay consistent with each other: the result isn't a rigid transform of the bone block, only a collection of pointwise displacements computed separately from one another. Don't reconstruct an overall movement from these numbers without checking them against each other first.

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: Clicking Apply reinstalls a dependency every time (legacy module)
text: Clicking Apply always forces a reinstall of numpy, even when everything was already working. That makes the run slower, and swapping out a core numerical library inside an already-running Slicer session can unsettle other tools that depend on it. If another module starts misbehaving after you've used SurgMovPred, restart Slicer before looking any further.

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: A missing column in the output isn't a crash
text: If one of the expected values is missing from the result, nothing errors out visibly: the model behind it was simply skipped because one of the columns it needed couldn't be found after the header cleanup. The warning stays in Slicer's log, not in the spreadsheet: if your output has almost no predicted columns, compare your headers against the example spreadsheet before looking elsewhere.

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: Check which sheet is active in your workbook
text: Only the first sheet of an .xlsx or .ods file is read. If your per-patient measurements aren't on the first sheet, SurgMovPred will read a different one, or an empty one, without saying so.

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: The test-files button doesn't fill anything in by itself (legacy module)
text: It does download an archive, but it only fills in the input and output folders if another module's test data (VFACE's) is already present on the machine. On a machine without it, clicking the button has no visible effect.

page: SurgMovPred: estimate the expected bone movement after surgery
title: All models are loaded on every run
text: SurgMovPred loads all 112 models into memory as soon as it runs, even for a single patient or a single value you actually care about: roughly 1.5 GB of RAM before it even reads your spreadsheet. Plan for that on a memory-constrained machine.

title: Two ways to run it
text: This page describes the legacy Slicer module. Using it through a VISOR server: see With VISOR and Using VISOR .

title: The heaviest module in the extension
text: VFACE is not a standalone tool: it's an orchestrator that chains, one after another, six other modules of the extension (resampling, orientation, bone segmentation, registration, dental surface segmentation, classification). On a batch of patients, expect the full run to be long , on the order of an hour per patient depending on your machine, and it keeps the other tools busy while it runs. Plan to launch it when you don't need the other modules at the same time, typically overnight on a series.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: Before using patient data
text: The VISOR client sends your files as they are on disk. Nothing is de-identified. See What leaves your machine .

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: MRI2CBCT is not shipped
text: MRI2CBCT stays out of the extension until it is ported to the server. The build file and the README both say so; it is not a module you can open in VISOR today.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: The key is stored in clear text
text: Slicer saves the key in its own settings file for your user, as plain text. The masked field only hides it on screen. Anyone who can read your Slicer settings can read the key.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: HTTPS has no fallback
text: There is no setting, flag or file that relaxes the HTTPS rule or the certificate check. An http:// address saved by an older version of the client is ignored at start-up.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: Stopping for review runs the blocking way
text: If you arm a "stop after" step (see Quality review ), the run does not use the detached mode: the server returns the review material in the answer to the original request. There the timeout from Server Tools Settings applies, and a lost connection loses the answer.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: VISU also works on any folder
text: You can open VISU on any folder a tool wrote, with no server involved: it pairs the scan, the masks, the surfaces and the landmarks of each patient by file name. The only thing it fetches from a server is hosted sample datasets.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: Nothing is de-identified
text: No de-identification tool exists in VISOR today. What you select is sent to the server as it sits on disk: file names, DICOM headers and every identifier they carry. A de-identification pipeline is specified in the client repository but its README states it is not implemented, and a search of the code finds no implementation.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: "The server URL must start with https://"
text: You typed an http:// address, or Slicer found one from an older version. Use the public https:// address; there is no way around the rule, including for a server on your own computer.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: 401: authentication failed
text: The key is wrong or missing. The panel can still say "Server: online" because the health page needs no key. Re-enter the key in Server Tools Settings and Save.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: 503 during a maintenance window
text: While the server is being updated, it refuses new work with a 503 and a Retry-After: 10 header, for at most 300 seconds. The client does not read that header: you see the server's message, or "Server error (503)". Wait and press Apply again. Reading results already under way is not blocked.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: 422: invalid arguments
text: The server names the offending argument, for example an option outside the accepted list. Fix the field it names. A "400" with a file-type message means the file extension is not accepted by that tool.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: 413: file too large
text: The server refuses an upload above its limit, 500 MB per file by default. For a large cohort, give a folder rather than one huge archive so that it can be split into batches.

page: Using VISOR: run the tools on a server from 3D Slicer
title: 500: "The tool failed on the server"
text: This is all the client shows for a crash inside a tool, on purpose: the details may contain server internals. Ask whoever runs the server to read its log.

title: Two code bases: legacy and VISOR
text: The tool pages listed below describe the legacy Slicer modules ( SlicerAutomatedDentalTools at 3c67957 , 2026-10-26). The team is moving the tools to VISOR : a Slicer client that sends the work to an inference server, where each tool runs in its own Python environment. Each module therefore has up to four pages. At the top of the sidebar, the Legacy | VISOR selector chooses the generation, and the Guide | Atlas selector below it chooses between the user's view and the code: legacy Guide, legacy Atlas, VISOR…

title: Coupling worth knowing
text: ALI , AREG , ASO , DOCShapeAXI and FlexReg share the same conda environment shapeaxi , on Python 3.12 . A change to the Python version breaks all of them at once. Details in FlexReg , Environment section.

title: Confirmed bug · a DICOM series folder gives a hidden output file
text: Select the folder of one DICOM series as the input (the case the panel invites) and the scan key becomes "." : _dicom_directories includes the root itself ( CB/dispatch.py:70-77 ), scan_key is os.path.relpath(root, root) ( CM/discovery.py:43 ), the converted file is named ..nii.gz ( CB/dispatch.py:156 , :164 ) and scan_stem("..nii.gz") is "." ( CB/engine.py:152-158 ). The output is ._lm_Pred.mrk.json , a hidden file. Run for this page: scan_key and scan_stem return exactly those values. A complete run on a real…

title: Pitfall · no reorientation to LPS
text: The legacy reorients every volume to LPS before the agents walk it, and says why in a comment: a volume stored in another orientation "reaches them mirrored" ( ALI_CBCT_utils/environment.py:66-72 ). VISOR does not. Run for this page against the real Environment.physical_position ( CB/environment.py:108-118 ): on a volume with identity direction and origin (-30,-25,-20), voxel (5,20,10) maps to (-25,-5,-10), the true point; on a volume with direction diag(-1,-1,1) and origin (30,25,-20), the function still returns…

title: Confirmed bug · ReLU on the last layer, kept from the legacy
text: The decision head ends in a ReLU ( CB/brain.py:90 ; legacy ALI_CBCT_utils/brain.py:35 ): the six scores are ≥ 0, and if all pre-activations are negative they are all 0 and argmax returns 0 , "up". Not to be "fixed" without retraining: the published weights were trained with this head.

title: Confirmed bug · the Slicer panel reports "0 scan(s), 0 landmark(s) written"
text: ALIRemote._summarize reads report.get("scans") (Remote ALIRemote/ALIRemote.py:216 ), but both engines write the per-scan records under cases ( CB/engine.py:708 , IO/engine.py:704 ). Nothing between them renames the key (the report merge in ServerToolsCore/ServerToolsCoreLib/base_widget.py:119 is generic). The end-of-run message therefore always says no scan and no landmark, and never lists the landmarks that did not converge ( ALIRemote.py:216-232 ). Run for this page: _summarize , extracted from the module…

title: Pitfall · the Mucogingival refinement stack is not ported
text: See What changed from the legacy logic . For the 13 mucogingival landmarks, the legacy at 3c67957 places each point, then smooths, snaps, completes and fills the line; VISOR places each one in a single pass and always estimates absent teeth ( IO/engine.py:354-358 ). The VISOR README reports one labelled lower arch: 13 landmarks out of 13, none forced, 12 identical to upstream and one 0.179 mm apart, and states that accuracy is not established for lack of annotated scans ( tools/ALI/README.md:292-300 ). What the…

title: Pitfall · two scans of the same stem overwrite each other
text: The output path is dirname(key)/<stem>_lm_Pred.mrk.json where the stem drops the extension ( CB/engine.py:916-921 ), so a.nii.gz and a.nrrd in the same folder write the same file with no error. Run for this page: scan_stem returns a for both names; the overwrite itself was not run.

title: Note · only Mucogingival points carry a description
text: O and C points, and every ALI_CBCT point, have an empty description whatever their quality: notes are filled only by the MG path ( IO/engine.py:567-575 , written by :426 ) and ALI_CBCT passes none ( CB/engine.py:921 ). The run report 's landmarks_degraded ( IO/engine.py:414-419 ) is the other place an MG doubt is recorded.

title: Note · noise in the IOS run report
text: ALI_IOS is handed the whole models folder, which also holds the CBCT checkpoints ( VISOR-serve scripts/data-manifest.yml:121-130 ), and lists every .pth whose name lacks a network token ( O , C , MG ) or a jaw token under models_unrecognized ( IO/engine.py:98-111 , :703 ). On a full bundle that is a long list of CBCT file names in every IOS report. Not a failure; not measured on the full bundle.

title: Note · dead duplicate in ALI_CBCT
text: CB/engine.py:644-650 and :651-657 are the same block (compute processed , raise "ALI produced no landmarks for any scan" if empty) twice in a row. No effect.

title: Verified · the O camera table is reproduced on purpose
text: Two O directions are divided by the norm of a different vector ( np.array([0.5, 0.0, 1.0]) / _norm([0.5, 0.5, 1.0]) ), so they have a length of 0.913 or 0.791 instead of 1 (calculated: 1.118/1.2247 and 1.118/1.414). The port keeps them deliberately, because the weights were trained on these views ( IO/render.py:8-12 , table :39-54 ; legacy ALI_IOS_utils/model.py:66-77 ).

title: Verified · independent landmarks, bounded searches
text: A landmark's result depends only on the scan, the weights and the seed, never on which other landmarks were requested ( CB/agent.py:54-68 ; this is what lets ASO ask for 7 and a standalone run ask for 119). Move bounds are tested coordinate by coordinate ( CB/agent.py:135-141 ) and both the search and the refinement stop on the same step counter ( CB/agent.py:238-243 , :272-286 ). The weights are loaded with weights_only=True ( CB/brain.py:133-135 ).

title: Scans are skipped silently when their name looks like an output
text: When scans is a folder, a file is left out if its name (without extension) contains _<prediction_ID>_ , ends with _MERGED , ends with one of the nine structure codes ( _MAND , _MAX , _CB , _CV , _UAW , _SKIN , _CBMASK , _MANDMASK , _MAXMASK ) or ends with _Seg or _SegOut ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:69-85 , applied at pipeline.py:111-113 ). A patient file called P01_CB.nii.gz or P01_Seg.nii.gz is therefore ignored. Only a count is logged, never the names ( pipeline.py:119-123 ); if every file is ignored, the run…

title: A split cohort keeps the report of its first batch only
text: When the panel splits a cohort, every batch writes AMASSS_report.json at the root of its own batch_NN/ folder ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:368 ). The client merges batch reports only for a module that names its report in RUN_REPORT ( AutomatedDentalToolsRemote ServerToolsCoreLib/base_widget.py:1493, 1559-1562, 2192 ); AMASSSRemote does not ( AMASSSRemote/AMASSSRemote.py:63-98 ), unlike AutoCrop3D, ALI, CNE, AutoMatrix, GreedyReg and DOCShapeAXI. When the batch folders are folded back, a name already present is kept…

title: Disk footprint: nothing is cleaned until the end
text: The tool keeps, for the whole run, an NIfTI copy of every scan ( nnunet_input , SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:387-388, 412 ) and one pred_<CODE> folder per structure ( pipeline.py:448 ). They are removed only by the rmtree of pipeline.py:366 . The legacy removed nnunet_input right after inference and each scan's predictions right after its assembly ( legacy AMASSS_CLI.py:872, 651-656 ). On a large cohort the peak disk use under output_dir is therefore higher than the legacy's; whether that is intended is not stated in…

title: GPU resampling lowers the input interpolation order, by default
text: gpu_resampling defaults to true. When it applies, the input data is resampled with torch in linear mode instead of nnU-Net's cubic spline: the code comment says this is the whole numerical difference with a stock nnU-Net run ( SADT-VISOR nnunet_runner.py:171-179 ). It is ignored on CPU, and left alone if the model plans request another resampler ( nnunet_runner.py:128-187 ). The report records the value requested on a CUDA device; a bundle whose plans opt out is only mentioned in the log ( pipeline.py:534-538 ).…

title: No GPU memory retry
text: The legacy retried an out-of-memory structure with scipy resampling ( legacy AMASSS_CLI.py:240-251 ). VISOR has no such handler: the structure goes to structures_failed in the report ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:475-478, 550 ), the run continues with the others, and fails only if all of them fail ( pipeline.py:484-488 ). With several structures now resident on the card at once (§5.3), the width the server grants is what keeps memory in bounds.

title: What the panel loads into the scene
text: Results are loaded only when the run produced 12 loadable files or fewer; above that, nothing is loaded and a dialog points to the folder ( AutomatedDentalToolsRemote AMASSSRemote/AMASSSRemote.py:82 ; ServerToolsCoreLib/base_widget.py:1596-1602 ). The patterns are *.nii.gz , *.nii , *.nrrd , *.nrrd.gz as label maps and *.vtk as models ( AMASSSRemote.py:92-98 ): a .gipl input, whose masks come back as .gipl.gz ( SADT-VISOR naming/src/sadt_naming/__init__.py:60 ), produces files that are saved but not loaded.

title: No shared working folder between runs
text: Each run works under its own <output_dir>/.amasss_work and removes it once inference has started, whether it succeeds or fails ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:59-62, 330-331, 342-366 ). The folder is created before the scans and models are looked up ( pipeline.py:331-336 ), so a run that finds no scan leaves it behind, empty. The two legacy bugs about a shared and wiped temporary folder ( legacy §6 and legacy §9 ) do not apply.

title: Structured report and early validation
text: The report lists the structures without a model, the structures that failed, and a status, an error and a duration per scan ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:497-558 ). Unknown structure or merge values are refused before any inference ( pipeline.py:306-327 ). The legacy CLI checks neither: an unknown structure becomes a missing model, and an unknown merge mode is caught scan by scan, after inference ( AMASSS_CLI.py:723-732, 623-627 ). cuDNN autotuning is switched off ( nnunet_runner.py:116 ); the code comment gives the…

title: No file name in logs or progress
text: The tool names a scan by its position in the batch or by its case id, in the log and in the progress messages the server stores and shows ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:116-118, 414-417, 584-587 ; progress.py:13-15, 100 ). The legacy logged the path of an unreadable scan ( legacy AMASSS_CLI.py:713 ). The file name is still in the report's cases[].input ( pipeline.py:399 ), which goes back to the caller with the results.

title: Models are never sent by the clinician
text: A model is published as a name, never as a file argument, so weights cannot be uploaded from a laptop ( VISOR-serve server/registry/conventions.py:14-16 ), and the argument is hidden in the AMASSS panel ( SADT-VISOR layout.py:32 ). See Security and privacy .

title: Elastix transform now exact
text: The centre of rotation is read and applied, and the unit tests recover a known rigid transform on a phantom ( cbct/elastix.py:212-240 , SADT-VISOR tools/AREG/AREG_CBCT/tests/test_elastix.py:50 ). Observed: pytest in the tool's environment, 101 passed.

title: Unpaired subjects are reported
text: A subject present at one time point only is listed under unmatched in AREG_report.json instead of vanishing ( cbct/dispatch.py:259-260 ). Read in code.

title: Oriented mode with the Occlusal reference
text: The legacy code derived the landmark list from the chosen reference ( AREG/AREG_Method/CBCT.py:629-630@3c67957 : six Occlusal landmarks or seven Frankfurt ones). The VISOR call to ASO sends none ( cbct/tools.py:93-107 ), ASO's default is the Frankfurt set Ba S N RPo LPo ROr LOr ( SADT-VISOR tools/ASO/src/sadt_aso/__init__.py:51 ), and ASO refuses a selection the reference cannot support, because the two published references carry disjoint landmark sets ( SADT-VISOR tools/ASO/src/sadt_aso/dispatch.py:435-458…

title: The scratch folder is not removed when a run fails
text: register deletes .areg_work/ after the engine returns, with no try/finally ( cbct/dispatch.py:397-460 , shutil.rmtree at line 455; the engine runs at lines 433-450), while its comment says it is removed whether or not the run succeeded ( cbct/dispatch.py:452-454 ). AREG_IOSCBCT has the finally ( SADT-VISOR tools/AREG/AREG_IOSCBCT/src/sadt_areg_ioscbct/dispatch.py:357-358 ). An exception that is not caught per patient would leave the copies of the inputs, the converted DICOM and the oriented T1 in the output…

title: Declared but unused
text: torch==2.8.0 is a dependency of the engine ( SADT-VISOR tools/AREG/AREG_CBCT/pyproject.toml:11 ) that no module of cbct/ imports (observed: grep for import torch and from torch , no match). The AREG README puts the whole environment sync, with CUDA wheels, at about 5.8 GB ( SADT-VISOR tools/AREG/README.md:143 ). In the shared package, common/scans.py is imported by no file of tools/AREG (grep, read in code); the extension table actually used is common/pairing.py:36 .

title: A docstring promises a mask rule the code does not have
text: The docstring of discover_masks says a file also counts as a mask “when it is the only candidate in a folder that holds nothing but masks” ( common/pairing.py:379-382 ). The loop accepts a file only when it carries both a segmentation token and a region token ( common/pairing.py:397-401 ). AMASSS's own names ( <scan>_seg_CBMASK ) satisfy both, so the automatic modes are not affected; a mask folder sent in Semi-Automated mode with names lacking either token finds no mask. Read in code.

title: The default patch height is 0, which means no band
text: run() publishes mgl_patch_height: float = 0.0 and documents it as “0 uses the engine's default” ( SADT-VISOR ios/__init__.py:36,65-66 ). The code does the opposite: only None is replaced by the 5.0 mm default ( ios/dispatch.py:395-397 ), and a height of 0 builds no curve and no band, only the snapped landmarks , which the ICP then uses alone ( ios/mgl.py:196-211 ; the check says “0 registers on the landmarks alone, without any band”, ios/dispatch.py:119-123 ). Observed: calling run() with the mucogingival patch…

The lower teeth kept out of the band are 18 to 31 in VISOR against 17 to 32 in the legacy, and the VISOR comment calls its range the upstream one, “verbatim” ( ios/mgl.py:66-72 ), which 3c67957 contradicts ( mgl_patch.py:47-55…

title: Duplicate faces lose votes in the palate network
text: In face_votes[:, view_faces[hit]] += view_probabilities[:, hit] ( ios/butterfly.py:157 ) an indexed addition does not accumulate repeated indices. Observed with torch in the tool's environment: adding ones to the same column three times in one indexed operation leaves 1. The legacy has the same accumulation ( AREG_IOS/AREG_IOS_utils/PredPatch.py:59-60 ); VISOR fixed the background pixels but not this. The vote is then written on the first corner of each face only ( ios/butterfly.py:161-166 ), which is why the…

title: Fully-Automated orients each jaw on its own
text: The call to ASO sends no ios_occlusion ( ios/tools.py:96-102 ), and ASO's default is “Orient each jaw independently” ( SADT-VISOR tools/ASO/src/sadt_aso/__init__.py:63-65 ). The registration then moves the other arch with the registered arch's matrix “so the captured occlusion survives” ( ios/pipeline.py:13-15,209-224 ), but if the two jaws were oriented separately, the occlusion captured in the scan is not what is carried. The legacy passed occlusion = "true" when the folder held lower arches…

title: No maximum on the patch height
text: The check refuses a negative height and nothing else ( ios/dispatch.py:119-123 ). The legacy widget kept the value in [0, 20] mm, ( AREG/AREG.py:42-44,870-882 ). Read in code.

title: The scratch folder is not removed when a run fails
text: register removes .areg_work/ after the engine returns, with no try/finally ( ios/dispatch.py:348-413 , shutil.rmtree at line 408; the engine runs at lines 385-403). An exception that is not caught per patient would leave the copies of the inputs and the labelled and oriented meshes in the archived output folder. AREG_IOSCBCT has the finally . Read in code; not triggered.

title: A failed orientation is written in the report
text: The patch is still predicted, but notes in the patient's entry say that it was predicted without the canonical orientation, with the reason ( ios/butterfly.py:117-131 , ios/pipeline.py:247-249 ). Read in code.

title: A transform is always written
text: Every registered patient gets a .tfm , in both modes and for both patches, with a sentence in the report saying which way it maps ( ios/pipeline.py:226-244 ). Read in code.

title: Crown_Seg is not told which device to use
text: label_crowns sends only meshes , suffix and an optional model ( ios/tools.py:124-130 ). Crown_Seg then uses its own default, with the server's device setting applied when the caller names none, and falls back to the CPU with a warning when no card is visible; see Crown_Seg on VISOR . Not a fault, an asymmetry with ALI_IOS, which passes its device on. Read in code.

title: The isosurface level can no longer be set
text: The legacy accepted AREG_CBCT_SURFACE_THRESHOLD ( AREG_IOSCBCT.py:92,943-950@3c67957 ). VISOR keeps the rule and the fallback of 400, and the warning it logs on falling back advises to “pass a level explicitly” ( ioscbct/volume.py:96-112 ), but the only caller never does: volume.read(scan_path, merged) ( ioscbct/dispatch.py:77 ) and run() has no such argument. Read in code.

title: On the published test scan the level is 1464, not 400
text: Observed with the tool's own functions on P_0001_T2_Or.nii.gz and its 12 CBCT landmarks: enamel 2783, soft tissue 146, level 1464 ( ioscbct/volume.py:96-117 ). At that level UL3O (brightest 274) is judged off enamel, and the landmark fit of the upper arch is made without it ( ioscbct/geometry.py:229-236 ). So “400” is only what VISOR uses when it cannot read a scan, and the surface any figure draws at 400 is not the one the VISOR ICP registers on. The viewer in 3.4 says so.

title: The documentation of max_dist is wrong
text: The docstring says that 0 uses 1.5, “which is upstream's” ( ioscbct/__init__.py:83-85 ). The code uses ICP_MAX_DIST_MM = 1.0 ( ioscbct/dispatch.py:352 , ioscbct/geometry.py:338 ), with a comment saying that upstream's signature says 1.5 and every call site passes 1.0 ( ioscbct/geometry.py:335-338 ). DEFAULT_MAX_DIST = 1.5 is the default of icp_point_to_point alone ( ioscbct/geometry.py:25,77-78 ), a function no module of the engine calls (grep: only tests/test_geometry.py does); the fallback the ICP actually uses…

title: A kept estimator describes an upstream that no longer exists
text: The docstring of icp_point_to_point says it was renamed from upstream's run_icp_point_to_plane because that function computes point-to-point ( ioscbct/geometry.py:81-86 ), and the comment above the ICP constants says it is kept as the fallback for a degenerate system ( ioscbct/geometry.py:331-334 ). At 3c67957 upstream's run_icp_point_to_plane has a real point-to-plane step ( AREG_IOSCBCT.py:579-608,719 ), and in VISOR the degenerate case falls back to _point_to_point_step , not to this function. Harmless, but…

title: The pre-alignment verdict is data, not a log line
text: Each mesh carries prealignment (accepted or not, why, landmarks fitted, residual, spread) and the ICP statistics, including the drift of the landmarks before and after ( ioscbct/pipeline.py:158-212 ). A volume that cannot be contoured does not stop the run: the meshes are placed on their landmarks and the report says that the ICP did not run ( ioscbct/dispatch.py:57-84 ). Read in code.

title: The scratch folder is always removed
text: Unlike AREG_CBCT and AREG_IOS, the engine wraps its work in a try/finally that deletes .areg_work/ ( ioscbct/dispatch.py:306-358 ). Read in code.
