title: Pitfall · the report does not record max_triplets or seed
text: The run() docstring says the report records them ( ASO/__init__.py:119-121 ); no key of that name is written anywhere in the tool's sources (the report is built in ASO/dispatch.py at :155-161 , :616-617 , :670 , :694 , :819 , :823 , :931 ). The tool README repeats the claim ( tools/ASO/README.md:166 ). Read in code.

title: Pitfall · max_triplets of 0 or less loses the whole CBCT batch with a misleading message
text: The sample is empty and best_triplet raises "Need at least three landmarks…" ( ASO/geometry.py:353-357 , :378-379 ); only RegistrationError is caught per CBCT patient ( ASO/dispatch.py:797 ), so the ValueError ends the whole run. Run for this page: two valid patients, Semi-Automated, max_triplets=0 : orient raises that ValueError and no patient is oriented. The argument is hidden, so only a direct API call reaches it.

title: Pitfall · IOS with an unusual tooth count fails late
text: Read in code, not run. Without a landmark file, a jaw is registered on tooth centroids, which needs exactly 3 or 4 teeth ( ASO/ios/pre_icp.py:26-29 ). The upstream check outside Fully-Automated mode only requires teeth times types of at least 3 per jaw ( ASO/dispatch.py:494-506 ), so 5 ticked teeth pass and each jaw then fails after its mesh was read.

title: Pitfall · the coordinate system of a landmark file is never checked
text: Also true in the legacy. load_landmarks reads each position as written ( ASO/markups.py:35-64 ); the only occurrence of coordinateSystem in the tool is the "LPS" it writes ( :75 ). A file exported in RAS is read with x and y inverted. Read in code.

title: Note · silent choices
text: When several scans share a patient folder, only the first, in sorted order, is kept, with no mention in the report ( ASO/cbct/pipeline.py:219-228 ; read in code, not run). The suffixes _Or and _OR are hard-coded when patient names are cut ( :34-36 ), whereas the output detection takes the caller's suffix ( :132-146 ). Run for this page: on a folder holding P1.nii.gz and P1_Reo.nii.gz , discover with output_suffix="Reo" returns two patients, P1 and P1_Reo (the earlier output, which would be oriented again), where…

title: Note · documents that no longer match the code
text: The tool README says "the server does not implement supervisors yet" ( tools/ASO/README.md:111 ); it does (VISOR-serve execution/runner.py:1685 ) and ASO uses one. VISOR-serve base.py:208 speaks of 130 landmarks for ASO where the signature has 115. A docstring of the Remote client says the mode is "asked for, never guessed" ( ASORemote/ASORemote.py:75-77 ), whereas automation is hidden ( ASO/layout.py:61 ); modality is the one asked for. segment_unlabelled still describes crown segmentation as "not implemented…

title: Verified · no GPU, no network, no torch in ASO itself
text: The ASO environment declares neither torch nor pytorch3d ( tools/ASO/pyproject.toml:8-21 ). The only GPU use of an ASO run is the prediction of ALI_CBCT, in Fully-Automated CBCT without supplied landmarks ( tools/ALI/ALI_CBCT/src/sadt_ali_cbct/__init__.py:95 , device = "cuda" by default).

title: Verified · a reproducible orientation
text: The triplet search is exhaustive up to max_triplets and seeded beyond it, with a local generator ( ASO/geometry.py:323-391 ); the legacy used the global np.random , so the same request could orient differently from one run to the next. The tool's tests compare the ported geometry with the legacy functions ( tools/ASO/tests/test_geometry_equivalence.py , part of the 205 tests run for this page).

title: Ollama is a prerequisite nobody deploys
text: The server tool needs an Ollama endpoint: the endpoint argument, else the OLLAMA_HOST variable, else the loopback address on Ollama's port 11434 ( SADT-VISOR tools/Agent/src/sadt_agent/llm.py:38-39,51-59 ). It never installs, starts or pulls a model ( llm.py:1-23 ), and a search of VISOR-serve for "ollama" finds nothing, so the image does not carry one. Without a reachable endpoint the tool raises ToolUnavailableError ( llm.py:86-91 ), which the server answers with a 503 ( VISOR-serve server/main.py:133-138 ).

title: A server tool with no client, a client with no server tool
text: The server tool is not reachable from any panel, and the client panel never contacts the server. Nothing in AutomatedDentalToolsRemote builds a request for Agent , and AgentRemote.py does not import ServerToolsCoreLib . The two share a name and a model tag, nothing else.

title: Execution is off by default, with three refusals
text: execute defaults to false ( __init__.py:43 ). When it is true, the run is still refused if no tool was chosen, if a required argument is missing, or if the confidence is below 0.5 ( routing.py:104-125 ). The source comment calls that threshold a floor against a model admitting it is guessing, not a quality bar ( routing.py:16-19 ).

title: No check at startup that the called tool exists
text: The call is written supervisor.run(...) instead of sup.run(...) on purpose, so that the schema generator does not record a fixed dependency ( execution.py:9-29,68-70 ). The names that reach it come from the catalogue, so a name is only as good as the registry it was read from. The catalogue does not exclude Agent ; a self-call would be refused by the supervisor's cycle check (VISOR-serve server/execution/runner.py:1814-1817 ), at run time.

title: Paths are still the model's word
text: The only paths the model sees are folders , and it is told to use them verbatim ( prompts.py:32-48 ), but nothing checks that a proposed path exists or is the right kind: the schema says path without saying file or folder, and the legacy extension check was dropped on purpose ( validation.py:9-17 ). The executed tool is what reports a wrong path. On a server, those paths are also server paths, not the user's. Read in the code.

Read in the code…

title: A scan named ..._Seg is invisible in a folder
text: With the default identifier, patient_Seg.nii.gz inside a folder is taken for an earlier output and ignored without any message ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:79-80, 104-105 ). A single file passed as scans is processed even if its name looks like an output ( pipeline.py:96-97 ).

title: GPU resampling is on by default and changes the numbers
text: When it applies, the input volume is resampled on the GPU in linear mode instead of nnU-Net 's cubic spline; the code states that this is the whole numerical difference and that gpu_resampling=false turns it off ( SADT-VISOR nnunet_runner.py:167-177 ). The report records the value requested on a CUDA device, and false on CPU; a bundle whose plans opt out is only mentioned in the log ( pipeline.py:374-378 ; nnunet_runner.py:163-165 ). The argument is hidden in the panel.

title: cuDNN autotuning is not switched off
text: BatchDentalSeg never sets torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark (no occurrence in the package), and nnU-Net's predictor sets it to true on CUDA ( nnunetv2/inference/predict_from_raw_data.py:60-61 , nnunetv2 as installed in the tool's environment). AMASSS switches it off explicitly ( SADT-VISOR AMASSS sadt_amasss/nnunet_runner.py:116 ). The tool's README says nnU-Net on CUDA is not bit-deterministic ( README.md:113 ): do not expect a bit-identical mask from two runs of the same scan.

title: An empty export list gives "ok" with no file (direct call only)
text: Called directly in Python, run(..., export_formats=[]) reports each scan as ok with an empty produced list and a summary "1/1 scan(s) segmented", and writes nothing ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:342-355, 362-386 ; mesh_export.py:187-189 ); the tool itself does not check the list. A request through the server is refused before the run, since the layout asks for at least one format ( layout.py:31-33 ; VISOR-serve server/base.py:855-858 ), and the panel asks for one too.

title: Per-label files depend on the NIfTI format
text: separate_segments splits the label volume, so it only works when NIFTI is selected: with meshes only, nothing is written for it even if the box is ticked ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:339-350 ).

title: The label table travels with the result, but Slicer does not read it
text: The report holds the full labels table ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:364-371 ). The Slicer panel defines no RUN_REPORT (default empty: ServerToolsCoreLib/base_widget.py:1493 ) and loads label volumes with a plain loadLabelVolume ( slicer_io.py:560 ); a comment in the module speaks of a colour table ( BATCHDENTALSEGRemote.py:79-82 ) but no code applies one.

title: One inference call: progress has two ends
text: The whole folder goes through one nnU-Net call, so the bar covers reading (0 to 10 %) and writing (90 to 100 %) and says "segmenting N scan(s) in one pass" in between, without inventing intermediate values ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:269-274, 301 ). An exception from that call fails the whole batch after cleaning the scratch folder ( pipeline.py:302-309 ).

title: An unreadable scan does not stop the batch
text: A scan that cannot be read is reported failed ("could not be read") and the others are segmented; only when none can be read does the run stop with an input error ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:273-298 ).

title: The backbone download is still reachable
text: The tool builds the network with maskrcnn_resnet50_fpn(weights=None) (SADT-VISOR tools/CLIC/src/sadt_clic/pipeline.py:136 ), as legacy did. In the pinned torchvision 0.26.0 ( pyproject.toml:14 ), weights_backbone defaults to ResNet50_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1 ( torchvision/models/detection/mask_rcnn.py:416 ) and resnet50(weights=weights_backbone) is called ( :490,502 ), which fetches the file through load_state_dict_from_url ( torchvision/models/_api.py:91 ); the checkpoint is loaded over it afterwards…

title: A scan with no detection is a success
text: A volume where nothing clears the threshold is written as an all-zero label map with "note": "no detection cleared the score threshold" ( __init__.py:245-249 ). The "nothing written" guard counts written scans, not detections ( :191-199 ), so a batch where every scan is empty is a successful run. The source comment says this is also what a wrong checkpoint looks like ( :246-248 ).

title: The client neither shows nor merges the report
text: CLIC_report.json carries the label table, what was detected and which scans failed ( __init__.py:133-155,173-186 ), but the panel has no RUN_REPORT (Remote CLICRemote/CLICRemote.py:53-72 ; base default empty, ServerToolsCore/ServerToolsCoreLib/base_widget.py:1493 ), unlike CNE and DOCShapeAXI . A scan that failed is visible only by opening the JSON. A folder larger than one batch (25 entries or 400 MB by default, VISOR-serve server/config.py:192,196 ) is sent as several runs whose folders are folded back into the…

title: Server comments describe another CLIC
text: VISOR-serve comments describe a CLIC that "batches slices inside one forward" ( server/execution/admission.py:146 ) with a batch_size = 4 argument ( server/execution/runner.py:1251,1271-1272 ), and quote memory measurements of CLIC at widths 1 to 45 ( server/execution/costs.py:470-477 ). The packaged tool has no batch_size argument, runs one slice per model([tensor]) call ( pipeline.py:170-176 ) and never calls progress.set_width , which is only defined ( progress.py:41 ). Those comments and figures therefore…

title: Overlaps are still resolved by order, slice by slice
text: Where two kept masks overlap on a slice, the one the network returned last overwrites the other, and each slice is decided alone: there is no vote between classes and no 3D consistency, so one canine can carry two labels on neighbouring slices ( pipeline.py:170-182 , same as legacy clic_runner.py:84-87 ). Read in the code.

title: The other legacy defects are gone
text: Checkpoint choice refuses ambiguity, the class count is read, loading is weights_only=True , outputs are named correctly and keyed by relative path so two homonymous scans no longer overwrite each other (SADT-VISOR __init__.py:40-73,223-231 , pipeline.py:96-144 ). The label table is in the report, not only in the widget.

title: The text of the notes is sent to the server
text: The legacy statement that CNE keeps clinical text on the machine ("no network exfiltration", legacy page §11 , and the legacy Guide's "Nothing leaves your machine" ) does not hold for VISOR . The VISOR panel uploads the notes you select to a tool server where the model runs (Remote README.md:24-35 ; CNERemote/CNERemote.py:57 and the server-side notes argument, Arguments and schema ). The Remote README says in so many words that there is no de-identification in the current client ( README.md:32 ), and the VISOR…

title: The client says "automatic", but nothing matches the model to the note type
text: The Remote README ("leave Model on automatic and the server uses the model fine-tuned for that note type", README.md:611-613 ) and the docstring of CNERemote/CNERemote.py:15-18 ("the model field defaults to (automatic)") are out of date. model is a required argument of the tool ( __init__.py:49 ), and the client adds its "(automatic)" entry only to optional arguments (Remote ServerToolsCore/ServerToolsCoreLib/base_widget.py:1074-1076 , rationale at formgen.py:107-109 ): the Model field lists the hosted bundles…

title: Only the TMJ model is hosted
text: The data manifest stages one bundle, TMJ/qwen-ft-q4_k_m.gguf (VISOR-serve scripts/data-manifest.yml:687-692 ). notes_type = "Ortho" is accepted by the tool but no Ortho model is hosted, and a model whose path names the other type is only a warning in the report, not a refusal ( __init__.py:133-139 , extraction.py:131-144 ). The manifest comment that the Ortho repository "answers 404 today" ( data-manifest.yml:682-686 , repeated in SADT-VISOR tools/CNE/README.md:205-208 ) is out of date: on 2026-11-09 an HTTP HEAD…

title: CPU, whatever some comments say
text: The pinned wheel index for llama-cpp-python is the CPU one (SADT-VISOR tools/CNE/pyproject.toml:60-67 ). Three comments disagree with it: the same file's header speaks of a "CUDA 12.4 wheel index below" ( :8-23 ); the published description of device says "it needs the CUDA build of llama.cpp, which this tool pins" ( __init__.py:82-84 ); and VISOR-serve's compose file says CNE cannot run in the CPU service because it ships the CUDA build ( docker-compose.yml:105-110 ). The code is the CPU build, so a cuda request…

title: No guard on the length of a note
text: The legacy concern about long notes (legacy page, §11 ) is only half closed. A cut-off answer is now refused ( __init__.py:293-297 ) and max_tokens defaults to 2048 instead of 500. But nothing compares the note with the context window or checks that max_tokens leaves room in it: context_for only rejects a negative value ( extraction.py:146-153 ). With the Ortho default the answer budget alone equals the window (2048 and 2048, :49 , __init__.py:51 ). What llama.cpp does then was not checked; whatever it raises…

title: Output names changed
text: Files are Extraction_<note file name>.json and .txt , not Extraction_<stem>.txt ( __init__.py:240-266 ). Anything that reads the legacy names, such as the legacy Dashboard ( Extraction_*.txt ), would not find the same files.

title: The silent legacy failures are closed
text: An image-only PDF, a truncated answer and an answer that is neither JSON nor fields now fail the note instead of writing a plausible file ( __init__.py:276-305 ); homonymous notes of different formats no longer overwrite each other ( :240-266 ); the TMJ/tmj spelling split is gone ( extraction.py:49-51 ); a GPU request that cannot be honoured is reported ( __init__.py:145-165 ). Read in the code.

title: No legacy module
text: The legacy repository (SlicerAutomatedDentalTools at 3c67957) contains no Crown_Seg module and no file with “crown” or “dentalmodelseg” in its path ( git ls-tree on that commit, observed). What it contains are calls to the CrownSegmentationcli module of the separate SlicerDentalModelSeg extension, and a small copy of the same call inside the ALI_IOS command line. The exact correspondence is in Legacy counterpart . How VISOR runs a tool on a server is described in Architecture .

title: FDI numbering over a mesh that is already labelled
text: With numbering = "FDI" and skip_segmented on, a mesh that already carries a label array is copied unchanged ( cs/pipeline.py:480-487 ; _write_as_vtk converts the file format, not the labels), while the report states array_name = "FDI_ID" and numbering = "FDI" ( cs/pipeline.py:556-561 ). The copy keeps its Universal integers under their Universal name, so the report announces a numbering the file does not hold. Observed: a synthetic mesh carrying a Universal_ID array was passed through segment_crowns with fdi=True…

title: Four names recognised here, three downstream
text: Crown_Seg treats a mesh as segmented if it holds any of PredictedID , UniversalID , Universal_ID or FDI_ID ( cs/pipeline.py:56 ). ALI_IOS, ASO and AREG_IOS read only the first three ( ali_ios/surface.py:19 , SADT-VISOR tools/ASO/src/sadt_aso/markups.py:19 , AREG_IOS/src/sadt_areg_ios/surfaces.py:39 ). A mesh that has only FDI_ID therefore passes Crown_Seg and is refused by the next tool: intended (the tool's own comment says so, cs/pipeline.py:64-80 ), but with no symptom before that next tool. The comment of…

title: Meshes in .vtp or .obj are invisible to Crown_Seg
text: Crown_Seg discovers .vtk and .stl only ( cs/pipeline.py:51,292-320 ), while AREG_IOS accepts .vtk .vtp .stl .obj as input ( AREG_IOS/src/sadt_areg_ios/surfaces.py:35 ) and, in Fully-Automated mode, hands its folder to Crown_Seg ( dispatch.py:172-173 ). A folder holding only such meshes is refused (“No surface mesh found in the input”, cs/pipeline.py:314-319 ); in a mixed folder they are left out of Crown_Seg's output, which is the folder AREG_IOS continues with. The legacy ALI_IOS copy of the call did read .vtp…

title: Two output trees: read the report
text: A segmented mesh lands under crownseg_input_<suffix>/ , a mesh that was already labelled lands beside its relative path, so a glob over one tree misses the other ( cs/pipeline.py:369-381,480-487 ). ALI_IOS reads cases[key].produced from run_report.json instead ( ali_ios/dispatch.py:240-252 ), which is what the report is for. A mesh of a degraded installation carries the status engine_unavailable yet is copied with its produced path ( cs/pipeline.py:495-505 ), so a client that filtered on already_segmented alone…

title: The tool graph in the server docs is out of date
text: VISOR-serve docs/TOOL_GRAPH.md:27-28,43 lists ALI_IOS as a leaf. The schema that ALI_IOS publishes declares calls = ['Crown_Seg'] (observed with scripts/describe.py in the ALI_IOS environment), because its dispatch calls Crown_Seg through a module constant ( ali_ios/dispatch.py:58,229 ). The document says it is generated from those schemas and checked at boot; the copy in the repository is older than the code.

title: Documentation that disagrees with the code
text: The README says that the model is a required argument ( README.md:33 ), and so does the docstring of the pipeline ( cs/pipeline.py:16-23 ); the argument is optional, with an empty default that resolves to the tool's own folder ( cs/__init__.py:41 , comment at cs/__init__.py:35-40 ). The README also names the folder DATA/CrownSeg/testfiles ( README.md:178 ) while the code and the manifest use DATA/Crown_Seg , and it counts 176 tests ( README.md:225,232 ) where 162 test functions are defined in tests/ (a def test_…

title: What the tool protects
text: The checkpoint is resolved before any file is created, so a refused request leaves nothing behind ( cs/pipeline.py:407-413 ); a folder that holds two checkpoints is refused with both named, so the vintage of the weights is never silent ( cs/pipeline.py:244-251 ); shapeaxi's standard output, which carries file names, is swallowed ( cs/pipeline.py:365 ); the scratch folder is removed in a finally ( cs/pipeline.py:435-439 ); the input is never modified. Read in code.

title: Reproducibility
text: The tool's README reports that the raw prediction PredictedID is bit-identical to a reference port, and that the post-processed Universal_ID varies from run to run, including between two runs of the same code (826 to 2,607 points of 294,260). This is the README's measurement ( SADT-VISOR tools/Crown_Seg/README.md:176-209 , section “Validated against”), not re-run here.

title: The EfficientNet backbone is a prerequisite nobody stages
text: shapeaxi builds an EfficientNet-B0 around every checkpoint . The tool refuses to let it be downloaded in the middle of a request, and instead raises FileNotFoundError unless efficientnet-b0-355c32eb.pth is already under <torch hub dir>/checkpoints/ (SADT-VISOR tools/DOCShapeAXI/src/sadt_docshapeaxi/pipeline.py:80-105 , called from load_network at :146 ; README.md:112-121 ). Neither the data manifest nor any script of VISOR-serve mentions this file (searched for "efficientnet" in the three repositories: only the…

title: The status line shows question marks
text: The client builds its summary from report.get("data_type") and report.get("checkpoint") (Remote DOCShapeAXIRemote/DOCShapeAXIRemote.py:122-130 ). The report written by the tool has neither key: it has model , anatomy , task , classes and network (SADT-VISOR __init__.py:97-110 ). The panel's summary will read "?" in place of the anatomy and of the checkpoint, while task and the surface count are filled. Read in the code, not run in Slicer.

title: The client describes a prediction table and a task selector that do not exist
text: The client's comments say the result is a "prediction table" in CSV form ( DOCShapeAXIRemote.py:76-86 ) and that a task argument narrows itself to the anatomy through an options_when rule ( :12-17 ). The tool writes no CSV ( __init__.py:97-110 ), and its schema has six arguments, none called task , with no options_when (output of scripts/describe.py ). The task is chosen by picking the checkpoint file, so a user must know what airways_2_class.ckpt and airways_4_regress.ckpt mean.

title: Two inputs with the same file name collide on output
text: Surfaces are found recursively but written flat: a/s.vtk and b/s.vtk both go to output_dir/s.vtk ( engine.py:111-112 ), so the second replaces the first, while the report keeps them apart by relative path ( __init__.py:84 ). The renaming step then moves s.vtk to s_pred.vtk once per entry ( __init__.py:128-132 ): the second move finds no file, which would end the run in a FileNotFoundError after all the computation; with an empty output_suffix the overwrite is silent. CLIC and CNE reproduce the input tree to avoid…

title: Still true from legacy: unseeded sampling, saliency of one branch only
text: No seed is set anywhere in the tool's sources and there is no seed argument, so the random point sampling inside shapeaxi ( engine.py:54,92 ) is not fixed from one run to the next, as in legacy (legacy page, pitfalls ). The Grad-CAM layer is the last block of the 2D views branch ( engine.py:82-83 ), so the map says nothing about the point-cloud branch. Read in the code.

title: Comments that disagree with the pins
text: The comment above the captum pin speaks of 0.9.0 while the pin is captum==0.8.0 ( pyproject.toml:39-44 ). The data manifest still labels the tool "NOT PORTED YET" ( data-manifest.yml:595 ). Neither changes what runs.

title: The legacy shapeaxi mismatch is fixed here
text: Legacy code is written for the shapeaxi 1.x API while its installer asks for 2.0.2 or later (legacy ADT/ADTLib/env/install_pytorch.py:385 ). VISOR pins shapeaxi==1.1.1 , with the reason in the comment ( pyproject.toml:18-30 ), and resolves the network classes from saxi_nets_lightning , where they live ( pipeline.py:135-145 ). The checkpoint is no longer copied into the output folder. Whether shapeaxi 1.1.1's EvalTransform honours scale_factor (the legacy page found shapeaxi ignoring it) was not checked.

title: "Patch and register" patches only the moving surface, not the reference
text: The patch is built on surfaces only ( SADT-VISOR __init__.py:155-157 ); the reference is read once and used as is ( __init__.py:121 ). The ICP selects the points of the patch array in both meshes ( ICP.py:70-72 ; pipeline.py:209-210 ). A reference without the Butterfly array fails with NoSegmentationSurf ( vtkSegTeeth.py:59-61 ), and an all-zero array with ToothNoExist ( vtkSegTeeth.py:75 ); neither is an input error, which matters for a batch: see the next finding. In practice, the reference must already carry…

title: Only input errors are reported per surface; other exceptions stop the whole batch
text: The loop catches ToolInputError only ( SADT-VISOR __init__.py:177 ), and the report is written after the loop ( __init__.py:191 ). Any other exception, such as the two raised by a reference without its patch, a tooth number outside 1 to 32 ( util.py:143-151 ) or a missing GPU in Dilation ( propagation.py:31 ), ends the run for every remaining surface and leaves no report. This is read from the code; it was not run.

title: "Mucogingival line" cannot be produced by anything in VISOR
text: The array Bottom_MGL ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:27 ) is created by no file of the tool nor of the Slicer client; the legacy built it in the widget ( legacy FlexReg_utils/mgl_patch.py:117 ). The panel still offers the choice ( __init__.py:53 ; layout.py:95 ). Register with it fails per surface if the mesh lacks the array ( pipeline.py:203-207 ). And Patch mode with the mucogingival line builds nothing: the construction is guarded by patch == "Palate (butterfly)" ( __init__.py:155-157 ), so the surface is copied and…

title: Without Universal_ID, the last array is used
text: When a mesh has no Universal_ID array, the tooth-label lookup falls back to GetLabelSurface , whose loop uses continue where break is needed and returns the last point-data array ( SADT-VISOR sadt_flexreg/util.py:25-28, 32-44 ). The legacy fixed this in ADTLib ( legacy FlexReg_CLI/FlexReg_Method/util.py:24-30 ). The Slicer preview takes the first single-component array instead ( FlexRegLib/butterfly_preview.py:136-152 ), while its comment says the server picks it the same way: preview and server can use different…

title: The four orientation teeth are fixed
text: The arch is oriented on teeth 3, 5, 12 and 14, whatever teeth are chosen for the corners ( SADT-VISOR make_butterfly.py:82-83 ); the client uses the same constants ( AutomatedDentalToolsRemote FlexRegRemote/FlexRegLib/butterfly_preview.py:29 ). An arch missing one of them fails even if the four chosen teeth exist. The four tooth_* arguments are hidden in the panel ( layout.py:101-104 ).

title: Joystick bounds are enforced by the server
text: Ratio in [0, 1], adjustment in [-5, 5] mm, translation in [-15, 15] mm ( SADT-VISOR layout.py:24-28, 57-59, 81-83 ); a value outside is refused ( VISOR-serve server/base.py:759-768 ). The comment in layout.py:22-23 still says a larger number typed in the box "still works": that is no longer true.

title: Output names can lie about the format
text: The output keeps the input extension ( SADT-VISOR __init__.py:163 ) but is always written as a binary legacy VTK file ( pipeline.py:90-94 ), so an .stl or .vtp input yields a file with that extension and a VTK content. Read from the code; what Slicer does with such a file was not checked. The legacy always wrote .vtk ( legacy FlexReg_CLI.py:321 ).

title: Absolute server paths in the report; GPU assumed for every mode
text: The report stores the absolute server path of the output and of the transform ( SADT-VISOR __init__.py:170, 175 ), although progress messages avoid file names on purpose ( __init__.py:144-146 ). And since the tool declares no device , the server queues even Register for the GPU ( VISOR-serve server/execution/dispatch.py:95-116 ).

title: The tool's documents misdescribe the legacy flip
text: The docstring of pipeline.py ( SADT-VISOR pipeline.py:8-14 ), the README ( tools/FlexReg/README.md:32-36 ) and the docstring of test_a_surface_leaves_in_the_convention_it_arrived_in ( tests/test_run.py:62-65 ) say that the legacy CLI flipped to RAS on read and never flipped back. At 3c67957 it does flip back before writing ( legacy FlexReg_CLI.py:295-305 ). The VISOR code is right; only the stated difference does not hold for that commit. Likewise the module docstring says curve and delete "stay in the Slicer…

title: The real patch construction has no test
text: The gpu marker is declared ( SADT-VISOR tools/FlexReg/pyproject.toml:32-34 ) but no test uses it, and the test of a missing tooth replaces butterflyPatch with a fake ( tests/test_run.py:336-349 ). The figures in the tool's README (patch on a 294,260-point arch) have no test behind them in the repository.

title: How references read on this page
text: SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/pipeline.py:74 is tools/GreedyReg/src/sadt_greedyreg/pipeline.py in SADT-VISOR at 6ba2a78; a bare pipeline.py , __init__.py or layout.py is the same package, a bare README.md or tests/… is under tools/GreedyReg/ , and pairing.py is tools/AREG/common/src/sadt_areg_common/pairing.py . VISOR-serve server/… is at e9a7e5d; AutomatedDentalToolsRemote … and a bare GreedyRegRemote.py or test_greedyreg_client.py (under GreedyRegRemote/ ) are at 19b95e8. Legacy references are files of…

title: The Slicer client describes a tool the server does not have
text: AutomatedDentalToolsRemote GreedyRegRemote/GreedyRegRemote.py:11-24 (docstring) and :50-57 (help text) describe a mode argument with Greedy , Landmark and Landmark + Greedy , a landmark_model and a second tool reached through the supervisor. The server tool has none of it: its run() takes t1, t2, output_dir, masks, initial_transforms, metric, transform_type, output_suffix ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/__init__.py:38-52 ) and a search for mode or " landmark " in the package finds nothing. The comment at…

title: The final status line reads a field that does not exist
text: _summarize formats {mode} from report.get("mode") and counts len(report["cases"]) ( AutomatedDentalToolsRemote GreedyRegRemote/GreedyRegRemote.py:133-138 ). The report has no mode (its keys are listed under Arguments and schema ), so the status-bar message reads "GreedyReg finished in ? mode: N pair(s) registered." And cases also holds failed patients ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/__init__.py:166-171 ), so N counts them. summary.registered is the right number.

title: Two files do not make a pair
text: The client says that two files are one pair ( GreedyRegRemote.py:75-77 ) and the fixture describes t2 accordingly. pairing.pair walks folders ( os.walk , pairing.py:232-276 ): run on 2026-11-09 with a/P1_T1.nii.gz and b/P1_T2.nii.gz it matched nothing, which the tool turns into No patient appears in both the T1 and the T2 folder ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/__init__.py:112-122 ). A single uploaded file reaches run() as that file's path ( VISOR-serve server/main.py:1288-1296 ). The tool's tests use folders only. A run…

title: The hosted test cohort is refused as offered
text: The only test file the server hosts for GreedyReg is CBCT_T1_T2_pair ( VISOR-serve scripts/data-manifest.yml:756-781 ), and every path argument offers it ( VISOR-serve server/registry/conventions.py:236-240 , no [tools.GreedyReg] section to narrow it). Its root holds a T1/ and a T2/ folder (checked on a staged copy). pairing.pair refuses a folder that holds more than one timepoint ( pairing.py:336-358 ), and GreedyReg does not descend into T1/ by itself, unlike AREG_CBCT which calls pairing.timepoint_root . Run…

title: Only the Greedy calls are bounded, not the run
text: Each Greedy call is limited to 600 s ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/pipeline.py:136,145 ) and a pair makes two ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/__init__.py:273,276 ), so a pair can take up to 1200 s. There is no bound on the number of pairs and the server sets none ( TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 0 , VISOR-serve server/config.py:77 ). VISOR-serve CLAUDE.md:896 speaks of a bound "per pair"; the code bounds each call.

title: No report when nothing was registered
text: If every pair fails, the tool raises ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/__init__.py:180-187 ) before the line that writes GreedyReg_report.json ( :189 ). The reasons then travel only in the error message. A failed patient's reason is the exception text ( :167 ).

title: The produced .mat is not a Slicer transform; the mask's space is not checked
text: <patient>_transform.mat is what Greedy writes with -o ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/pipeline.py:86 ; __init__.py:255 ); nothing in the package converts it to a .tfm , and the client does not load it ( GreedyRegRemote.py:97-104 ). A multi-label mask is flattened by > 0 and nothing checks that it lies in the space of T1 ( pipeline.py:117-126 ). Both points are those of the legacy module ( legacy page ), carried over unchanged. Read in code.

title: Defaults that differ from the legacy module
text: The metric default is NCC where the legacy combo started with NMI ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/__init__.py:49 , GreedyReg.py:575@3c67957 ), the transform is Rigid by default, and the suffix is configurable ( output_suffix ) where the legacy CLI wrote _registered ( GreedyReg_CLI.py:168@3c67957 ).

title: Greedy is assumed to use the GPU
text: The tool declares no device argument, so the server's admission treats every run as a GPU run ( VISOR-serve server/execution/dispatch.py:95-116 ), while Greedy runs on the CPU. A GreedyReg run can therefore wait for a GPU slot it does not use. Read in code.

title: Pairing and failures are explicit
text: Unmatched patients, unused masks and unused initial transforms are reported ( SADT-VISOR GreedyReg/__init__.py:108,131-132 ); one failing patient costs one patient; the metric and the transform type are validated twice ( pipeline.py:47-55 ). The 189 tests of the package passed on 2026-11-09, with Greedy stubbed.

title: The listed model belongs to the old module
text: The manifest comment says the TMJ crop network is "fetched by MRI2CBCT's install_nnunet() " (VISOR-serve scripts/data-manifest.yml:708 ). That function exists only in the unbuilt client copy ( MRI2CBCTRemote.py:1244 ). In the legacy rewrite, the matching constant TMJ_CROP_MODEL is referenced by nothing (legacy ADT/ADTLib/model_registry.py:70 ; see the legacy page's dead-code list ). Placing that file on a server does not prepare a port of the current module.

title: Not the de-identification of what VISOR uploads
text: This module anonymises text documents that you point it at. It is not placed in the upload path of any other panel, and no code of ServerToolsCore , SlicerCloud or ServerToolsSettings mentions Presidio or anonymisation. The client README states that there is no de-identification in the current client: files are streamed "as they are on disk, with their names, their DICOM headers and whatever identifiers they contain" ( README.md:32-35 ), and the client shows the same warning once for each remote server, "Files…

title: Unnamed index column in both tables
text: Both result files start with a column holding 0, 1, 2 and so on, before IDPatient ( pipeline.py:283-284 ). The legacy CLI does the same (legacy SurgMovPred_CLI/SurgMovPred_CLI.py:268-269 ). Account for it when reading column positions.

title: Stale comments in the client
text: The client says output_kind "is file" (Remote SurgMovPredRemote/SurgMovPredRemote.py:44 ) and the base widget gives "SurgMovPred's single predictions_outputs.xlsx" as its example (Remote ServerToolsCore/ServerToolsCoreLib/base_widget.py:1390-1391 ). The tool returns two files, which the schema code publishes as a set of files (VISOR-serve server/registry/schema_tool.py:100-103 ). The panel still handles them, since it unpacks any zip it receives.

title: Stale data path in the README
text: The tool README gives the model folder as /DATA/SurgMovPred/models ( README.md:45 ), while the code looks under Surg_Mov_Pred ( __init__.py:19,34 ), the name the data manifest also uses (VISOR-serve scripts/data-manifest.yml:91 ). The code is the reference.

title: Still true from legacy: independent targets, nothing applied to the scene
text: Every target is a separate model.predict on the same row ( pipeline.py:216-247 ), so the predicted displacements of points of one rigid segment are not constrained to agree with each other (legacy page, pitfalls ). The output is the two tables only: no transform, no Slicer node, and the panel saves the archive rather than loading anything ( RESULT_KIND = "save_as" , Remote SurgMovPredRemote.py:46 ). Read in the code.

title: A skipped target is visible only in the server log
text: A package whose features are missing from the table is skipped with a logger.warning , and a target that fails to predict with logger.exception ( pipeline.py:234-236,249-250 ). The run then succeeds with fewer columns. There is no report file, so the user sees the missing targets only by counting columns. The one guard is the all-or-nothing case ( :252-264 ). Read in the code.

title: Reproducible order and no silent empty result
text: Packages and tables are sorted, so two runs on the same input give the same rows and columns in the same order ( pipeline.py:143-147,173 ); a run where no model predicts is an error, not two empty tables ( :252-264 ); a bad column name is an error, not a shadowed feature ( :51-60 ). Read in the code.

title: A port on two feature branches
text: The VFACE tool exists only on the branch tool/vface of SADT-VISOR (6ba2a78, 22 commits ahead of main ), and its server section [tools.VFACE] only on the branch conf/vface-deployment of VISOR-serve (e9a7e5d). git ls-tree main tools/ on SADT-VISOR lists no VFACE folder, and the deployment.toml of VISOR-serve's main has no VFACE section. A server built from the main branches does not publish VFACE, even though the Slicer module VFACERemote is on the client's main . Everything below describes those two branches.

title: Never run with its six real callees
text: The README states that no supervised chain has been executed with the six tools: the calls are covered by a fake supervisor asserting the parameters, plus a test that reads the six published schemas. It also states that nothing has been compared with the legacy output on a patient, and that nothing is validated clinically ( README.md:184-193 ). The 174 passing tests ( README.md:183 ) are evidence for the arithmetic and the wiring, not for a patient's result.

title: Heat maps: Batch_Dental_Seg is not asked for surfaces
text: segment_surfaces sends Batch_Dental_Seg only scans , model and prediction_ID ( SV:tools.py:359-364 ). Batch_Dental_Seg's export_formats defaults to ["NIFTI"] ( SADT-VISOR tools/Batch_Dental_Seg/src/sadt_batchdentalseg/__init__.py:22-24 ), and a mesh is written only for a mesh format in that list ( pipeline.py:342-353 of the same package). VFACE then looks for .vtk and .vtp only ( SV:heatmap.py:29, 194-204 ), finds no pair, and refuses with "No heat map could be drawn" ( SV:heatmap.py:246-251 ). Read in code, not…

title: Heat-map outputs have no surface bundle on this deployment
text: The server file says " surface_model is Batch_Dental_Seg's, and this deployment publishes none" ( VS:server/deployment.toml:277-279 ). The tool does not look for one in DATA ( surface_model is not in SV:dispatch.py:315-323 ), the panel hides the field ( SV:layout.py:100-104 ), and a request for heat maps without it is refused with "Heat maps are drawn on segmented surfaces, and 'surface_model' names the bundle that makes them" ( SV:dispatch.py:452-458 ). Read in the code, not executed: the two outputs that…

title: A longitudinal study is also classified
text: In VISOR, _classify runs whenever measurements are asked for, whatever the study ( SV:dispatch.py:521-533 ). The legacy built the feature table and ran the classifier only for an asymmetry assessment ( clp:1141-1175 ). In a longitudinal study the features are T1-to-follow-up differences, while the models were trained to read a patient against their mirror, so the Asymmetry column of such a run has no stated meaning. Read in code, not executed.

title: Cohort batching splits t1 and not t2
text: The server splits a cohort on the single required path argument ( VS:server/registry/conventions.py:158-188 ). For VFACE that is t1 : t2 and registration_transforms are optional, and the bundles are excluded as models. The comment of batch_axis_for excludes tools with two required paired folders, but nothing excludes a pair whose second folder is optional. So a longitudinal cohort above 25 files or 400 MB would be cut along t1 with t2 left whole or unsplit, depending on what the client sends with each batch.…

title: Error advice points to fields that do not exist
text: When a callee is missing, the refusal tells the user to send "your own segmentation masks in 'masks'" and "your own landmark files in 'landmarks'" ( SV:tools.py:53-56, 66-69 ). The signature has no masks and no landmarks argument ( SV:__init__.py:22-49 ).

title: The data manifest still says "NOT PORTED YET"
text: VS:scripts/data-manifest.yml:654 labels VFACE "NOT PORTED YET", although the tool exists on tool/vface and has a server section. The manifest also lists only V_FACE_Models.zip , DefaultList.zip and Testing.zip ( :656-673 ), whereas the tool resolves six bundle folders under DATA/VFACE/models/ ( SV:dispatch.py:315-323 ). Do not use the manifest to tell what is served.

title: Six callees, not seven; a cap of ten, not five
text: Comments say VFACE orchestrates "seven tools" ( VS:server/deployment.toml:258 ; R:VFACERemote/VFACERemote.py:14 ). The tool calls six ( SV:tools.py ), and its published schema lists six. SV:tools.py:17-20 and README.md:111-113 give the runner's nesting cap as five; the server at e9a7e5d sets MAX_SUPERVISOR_DEPTH = 10 ( VS:server/execution/runner.py:196 ), and its comment still names AREG_IOSCBCT, ASO, ALI_CBCT, three levels, as the deepest real chain ( runner.py:185-189 ), where VFACE's is four.

title: The heat-map branch finds registered scans in AREG's folder
text: draw_cohort hands Batch_Dental_Seg the region folder that _region_folder selected for its transforms ( SV:heatmap.py:224-226 ; SV:tools.py:236-262 ). AREG_CBCT writes the registered scan and its transform side by side in that folder ( SADT-VISOR tools/AREG/AREG_CBCT/src/sadt_areg_cbct/pipeline.py:72-83 ), so the folder does hold volumes to segment. Read in code, not executed.

title: Arithmetic parity is tested
text: The distances, angles, sign blocks and statistics tables are transcribed from the legacy code and compared with this port on random input: 6,200 distances, 3,000 angles, 65,536 dental distance labels and others ( README.md:166-172 ; tools/VFACE/tests/test_matches_upstream.py ). This was read from the README and the test file, not re-run for this page.

title: A stale source_hash is not fatal, whatever docs/INTERNALS.md says
text: VISOR-serve docs/INTERNALS.md lists "a stale source_hash " among the failures that stop the server. The code does the opposite: resolve_schema compares the cached schema's hash with the hash of the tool's src/ and, on a mismatch, regenerates the schema with the tool's own describe.py run in the tool's interpreter ( server/registry/schema_tool.py:234-266 ). Only a describe.py that returns a schema whose hash still does not match raises SchemaError , and discovery catches that and records it as a single failed tool…

title: A warning that is logged for keys the server does use
text: describe.py emits review_kind and case_input ( SADT-VISOR scripts/describe.py:1177-1182 ), and SchemaTool reads both ( VISOR-serve server/registry/schema_tool.py:762, 766 ), but neither is in _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS ( :162-165 ). The check at :690-697 therefore logs "ignoring unknown schema key(s)" for every tool that declares them: ALI_CBCT and ALI_IOS ( REVIEW_KIND = "landmarks" ) and ASO ( CASE_INPUT = "input" ). The values are consumed (the kind of a stop point, and the replay of corrected cases), so the message is…

title: The supervisor parameter is invisible to the schema
text: A run() receives the supervisor through a keyword-only parameter named sup with no annotation ; data_root works the same way. describe.py ignores both on purpose and publishes "supervisor": true instead ( SADT-VISOR scripts/describe.py:71-81, 731-752 ). The missing annotation is the marker.

title: Documentation behind the code
text: Three statements about the schema in the repositories' own documents no longer hold. The header of schema_tool.py says a schema cannot express extensions, choices, a section, a label or visible_when ( :28-33 ); all five are in _ARGUMENT_KEYS . SADT-VISOR CONTRIBUTING.md:154-169 and docs/SERVER_CONTRACT.md:41-48 speak of "six" layout keys and say options_when is not emitted; LAYOUT_KEYS has eighteen and includes it. CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md do not mention vec2 , nor that every argument needs a line in Args: .

title: The file is not "empty"
text: VISOR-serve server/README.md:540 calls deployment.toml "an empty file of comments today", and its own first lines say it "has no entries" ( server/deployment.toml:1-4 ). It has fourteen sections. The conventions of the previous section cover the generic case; these sections are the exceptions that were needed.

title: Stale example in a docstring
text: The module docstring of facade.py:14 still shows a mode named "CBCT to IOS" ; the mode that exists is "IOS to CBCT" .

title: docs/TOOL_GRAPH.md is out of date
text: VISOR-serve docs/TOOL_GRAPH.md draws the AREG engines and ASO , marks ALI_IOS as a leaf ( :27 ), omits VFACE , and states that the deepest real chain has three levels, AREG_IOSCBCT → ASO → ALI_CBCT ( :53 ). In the code ALI_IOS calls Crown_Seg and the deepest chain has four levels, through VFACE . Agent is outside the graph by construction: it calls tools through supervisor.run(…) , not sup.run(…) , so that describe.py , which insists on a literal name, does not fail on it ( SADT-VISOR…

title: MRI2CBCT is not delivered
text: MRI2CBCTRemote and MRI2CBCT_CLIRemote stay in the tree but have no add_subdirectory ( Remote CMakeLists.txt:31-32 ), and the extension description says "MRI2CBCT is temporarily not shipped until it is ported to the server" ( :10 ). SADT-VISOR has no MRI2CBCT tool. What is left is the legacy local code ( slicer.cli.run , a pip_install of torch ), unreachable from a built extension. See the VISOR page of MRI2CBCT and its legacy page for that code.

title: The documents count the members wrong
text: The docstring of the class says "six members" ( runner.py:1686 ), VISOR-serve docs/INTERNALS.md:80 says "five members, frozen" and server/README.md:652 "five members", and SADT-VISOR scripts/run_tool.py implements a local supervisor with five ( run, out, tmp, progress, log ; run_tool.py:300-364 ) that has no cycle check, no depth limit and no declareQualityControl . The server has eight, listed above. server/README.md:660 also says "five deep is the backstop"; the constant is 10.

Citations are file:line in VISOR-serve at commit e9a7e5d , which is main ( e91557e ) plus one commit that touches only server/deployment.toml (it declares the VFACE data folder). The tools themselves are in SADT-VISOR at 6ba2a78 . “Legacy” on this site means the Slicer modules of SlicerAutomatedDentalTools; nothing below applies to them. What section 7 says about a running instance comes from an inspection dated 2026-10-20, not from the code. Transport protection, tokens and the data-handling claims are on the…

Documentation inside the repository still describes older images. The Dockerfile comment at :193-195 says server/tools/ is excluded by .dockerignore , which is no longer true ( .dockerignore:18-30 ). The comments at :11-12 and :217 still count fifteen tools or upstreams; there are 19 packaged tools. docker/README.md:45-48 says a tool nested one level deeper “is NOT discovered by the server today”, yet discovery is two levels deep and five served tools ( ALI_CBCT , ALI_IOS , AREG_CBCT , AREG_IOS , AREG_IOSCBCT )…

The compose default ${API_TOKEN:-dev-token} means an installation that does not write a .env runs with a token that is public, because it is in a versioned file. The port mapping "${BIND_ADDR:+${BIND_ADDR:-}:}${VENVS_HOST_PORT:-8001}:8000" ( docker-compose.yml:224 ) publishes on every interface when BIND_ADDR is unset. The path through scripts/server_ctl.py generates a token and defaults BIND_ADDR to 127.0.0.1 ( server_ctl.py:368,398 ); starting compose by hand does not.

title: The file is not empty, whatever its header says
text: server/README.md:540 says deployment.toml “is therefore an empty file of comments today”, and the first lines of the file itself say “this file has no entries” ( server/deployment.toml:1-4 ). Both are false at this commit: the file has 14 sections, which is what makes the AREG and ALI facades, the VFACE data folder and the per-tool batch and width declarations work.

title: A dated observation, not a property of the code
text: One running instance was inspected on 2026-10-20 (a report kept outside the repositories). What it found about that machine may no longer be true. This section keeps what the code explains; the details that identify the machine or its network are deliberately left out. The only check made while writing this page was an unauthenticated GET /health and GET /tools : they answered {"status":"ok"} and 23 entries.

Read these numbers for what they are. They were measured from 2026-08-25 on a single machine (Xeon w7-3555, 28 cores, 125 GiB, RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, driver 595.84, 1 Gb/s Ethernet, Ubuntu 22.04.5), on a single card, with MAX_CONCURRENT_GPU_JOBS=1 ( benchmarks/README.md:338 ), that is, before the admission engine replaced that counter (commit 89393b5 , 2026-09-21). They were taken on loopback or local only, so the transfer times are those of localhost , not of a network. Their records point to tool and server trees…

Byte-for-byte parity between the local path and the HTTP path is established for one tool, AREG_IOSCBCT , in one session (n = 1 pair). It is not established in general. The control shows that most of these tools do not even reproduce themselves byte for byte on the same path, because their reports carry durations or paths, and a byte comparison does not tell a report from data. Neither “parity reached” nor “parity lost” can be written from this table. The repository's README says the harness reproduces every…

title: The end-of-run message says "0 scan(s), 0 landmark(s) written"
text: Whatever happened. The panel looks for the list of scans under a name that the server no longer uses ( ALIRemote.py:216 in AutomatedDentalToolsRemote 19b95e8, against cases in the server report). Read the files that were loaded and the run_report.json in the result folder instead; the failures are listed there, and the panel message never lists them.

title: Choosing the folder of a single DICOM series
text: If you point to the folder that holds exactly one DICOM series, the result file is named ._lm_Pred.mrk.json , a hidden file, and will not show in a normal file listing. Put the series in a sub-folder of the folder you choose, or show hidden files. The cause was checked in the code (the two naming functions were run); a full run on a real series was not repeated.

title: CBCT stored in another orientation
text: The legacy module turns every CBCT to a standard orientation ( LPS ) before the search. The server version does not. The effect on the placed points has not been measured, so look at the landmarks on the scan before using them, particularly if your volume does not come from a DICOM export.

title: A scan can be skipped without a message
text: When you give a folder , files whose name ends in _CB , _MAND , _MAX , _CV , _UAW , _SKIN , _CBMASK , _MANDMASK , _MAXMASK , _MERGED , _Seg or _SegOut , or that contain _Pred_ (your prediction identifier), are taken for earlier AMASSS outputs and left out. Only a count is logged, not the names. If you named a patient's scan P01_CB.nii.gz , rename it, or pass that file on its own: a single file is never filtered. (Reference: SADT-VISOR sadt_amasss/pipeline.py:69-132 .)

title: Graphics memory
text: If the server's graphics card runs out of memory on a structure, that structure is missing from the result and listed as failed in the report; the legacy module retried it with the resampling done on the CPU. The run only fails if every structure fails (SADT-VISOR sadt_amasss/pipeline.py:475-488 ).

title: Oriented mode: choose the Frankfurt reference
text: The orientation step asks ASO for its default landmarks , the Frankfurt set, whatever reference you picked. The Occlusal reference carries other landmarks, and ASO refuses a combination it cannot support. If you pick the Occlusal reference in this mode, expect that refusal. This was read in the code; the chain was not run.

title: Type a patch height for the mucogingival patch
text: The field Patch height (mm) starts at 0 , and 0 does not mean “use the default”: it means no band at all, so the registration uses only about 13 landmark points. The legacy module started at 5 mm. Type a height (5 is the engine's own default) before you press Apply. There is no maximum, so keep it within the attached gingiva. The value used is written in the report. Observed by calling the VISOR tool: a run without a height reaches the engine with 0.

title: Patient names that differ only by letters are merged
text: The two modalities are paired on the digits of the patient identifier, leading zeros removed. A12 and B12 are the same patient for the tool, and so are P001_T1 and P001_T2 . Observed by running the VISOR pairing code: with the meshes of both time points of one patient and several CBCTs for the same digits, a single patient was formed, only the first CBCT in sort order was used and the others vanished without a word, and a T2 mesh was given the landmarks of the T1. Send one patient, one time point and one CBCT per…

title: A landmark file with the wrong name is replaced, without a message
text: If a scan has a landmark file that does not pair with it by name (for example P1.mrk.json next to P1_CBCT.nii.gz ), the server cannot see it, predicts new landmarks instead and orients on those, even in the semi-automatic setting. The report says the landmarks came from ALI_CBCT and lists no unmatched file. This was reproduced with the tool's test helpers (and without a prediction tool the same input fails and names the file). Name your landmark files after the scan (the failure message names the rule, built on…

title: Intraoral, five teeth ticked
text: Without a landmark file, the coarse alignment needs 3 or 4 teeth per jaw. With 5 ticked, the request is accepted and each jaw fails afterwards (read in the code; not run).

title: A server-side Agent exists, but no panel offers it
text: The VISOR server can host an Agent tool that proposes which server tool to run for a request, and runs it only if asked to. It needs an Ollama server that the administrator has set up separately, and no panel in the client calls it ( SADT-VISOR tools/Agent , commit 6ba2a78). For how it works, see the VISOR Atlas page for Agent .

title: A mesh needs a segmentation-like file name
text: With the default surfaces = segmentations , a file called P1_Seg.nii.gz gets a mesh and a file called Mandible.nii.gz does not (checked on 2026-11-09 against the port's own rule). A folder name does not count. Rename the file, or set surfaces to all . The mesh is placed in the scan's own space, so it lies over the cropped scan in Slicer.

title: The final status line is wrong
text: The message shown in Slicer's status bar when the run ends always says "AutoMatrix: 0 file(s) written.", and never mentions unpaired files. It reads two fields that the report does not have. Judge the run from the output folder and from AutoMatrix_report.json ( summary.files_written , without_a_transform , transforms_without_a_file ).

title: Without a reference volume the result can land beside the data
text: The panel offers no reference volume. With none, the output keeps the input size but takes the transform's image of the origin as its origin. Tested on 2026-11-09 by calling the server's tool directly with a substitute reflection matrix on a small volume centred on the origin: the output was empty, and it was complete when the volume was its own reference. A plain translation also shifts the content and can cut part of it. This is what the mirror box uses. A fix exists on an unmerged branch…

title: A scan named ..._Seg inside a folder is ignored
text: With the default identifier, a file such as patient_Seg.nii.gz found in a folder is taken for an earlier result and skipped, with no message. Rename it, or select that file on its own: a single file is always processed. (Reference: SADT-VISOR sadt_batchdentalseg/pipeline.py:72-107 .)

title: Resampling on the GPU
text: By default the server resamples the scan on the GPU, which changes the numbers very slightly compared with nnU-Net 's own resampling. The report field gpu_resampling says whether it was requested on a GPU. Because the setting is hidden in the panel, ask the server administrator if you need the exact nnU-Net pipeline.

title: An empty result is not an error
text: When nothing clears the threshold on a scan, you get an all-zero segmentation and the run is reported as successful, even if it happens on every scan of the folder. The report carries the note "no detection cleared the score threshold" for each such scan. An empty result can be a true answer or a wrong model, so read the report before concluding that there is no impacted canine.

title: Your notes are uploaded
text: The text of the notes you select leaves your workstation and is read by the server. The current client does not de-identify anything before sending, so the legacy guide's "Nothing leaves your machine" does not apply here. Remove identifying information first, and only use a server your institution has approved for clinical text. What is and is not protected is on Security and privacy in VISOR .

title: Give each surface a distinct file name
text: Surfaces are searched in subfolders but the results are written side by side. Two files called surface.vtk in different subfolders are written to the same place: one replaces the other, and the run is then likely to stop with an error after all the computation is done. This is deduced from the code, not tested.

title: A new server may refuse its first run
text: The network needs a small image-model file (an EfficientNet backbone) that the tool will not download in the middle of a request. If it has not been put in place on the server, the run fails after your meshes have been uploaded, with a message naming the missing file. That is a server setup problem: send the message to whoever runs the server.

title: The reference must already carry its patch
text: In "Patch and register", the patch is built on the arch you register, not on the reference. Both meshes must have the patch: build it on the reference first (mode Patch on that arch), then use the result as the reference. Otherwise the run stops with an error that is not reported per arch, and a batch ends without a report. (Reference: SADT-VISOR sadt_flexreg/__init__.py:121, 155-157, 177 , read from the code, not run.)

title: The mucogingival line cannot be created by VISOR
text: Choosing "Mucogingival line" only works on a file that already has that region marked. Nothing in VISOR computes it, and in Patch mode that choice copies your arch unchanged and still reports success.

title: Give two folders, even for one pair
text: The client says that two files make one pair, but the pairing walks folders: tested on 2026-11-09 with a/P1_T1.nii.gz and b/P1_T2.nii.gz , nothing was paired, and the tool's error is "No patient appears in both the T1 and the T2 folder". Put each scan in its own folder. A test through a server was not made.

title: The hosted test cohort: pick its T1 and T2 sub-folders
text: The test file a server offers for GreedyReg, CBCT_T1_T2_pair , holds a T1 and a T2 folder. Given as a whole for T1 and T2, it is refused ("The T1 folder holds scans from more than one timepoint"); its T1 and T2 sub-folders pair. Checked on 2026-11-09 on the file names of a staged copy; whether the panel lets you pick a sub-folder of a hosted file was not checked. The masks and initial-transform rows offer hosted test files too: give your own.

title: The final status line is not reliable
text: When the run ends, Slicer shows "GreedyReg finished in ? mode: N pair(s) registered." The report has no mode, and N counts failed patients too. Read GreedyReg_report.json ( summary.registered and summary.failed ) instead.

title: A slow pair fails after ten minutes per step
text: A registration is two Greedy steps and each is cut at 600 s, so one pair can take up to twenty minutes. The server sets no limit on the whole run. A pair cut short appears as failed in the report with the exception text as its reason.

title: It does not de-identify what VISOR uploads
text: When you run a tool on a VISOR server, your image files are sent as they are on disk, with their names and DICOM headers ( AutomatedDentalToolsRemote README.md:32-35 ). This module does not touch them, and the client has no de-identification step at the moment; the extension says so once for each remote server, with the message "Files are uploaded unmodified". Read De-identification in VISOR before sending patient data to a server.

title: Two cases now stop with an error
text: If a header cannot be cleaned into a column name, the run stops and names the column ( VISOR:SADT-VISOR tools/Surg_Mov_Pred/src/sadt_surgmovpred/pipeline.py:57 ). If no model at all can predict from your table, the run stops with an error instead of producing empty files ( pipeline.py:260 ). A table that only lacks some columns still yields fewer predicted columns without an error.

title: Only on servers built from two feature branches
text: The server side of VFACE exists only on development branches (SADT-VISOR tool/vface and VISOR-serve conf/vface-deployment ), not on their main . A VISOR server built from main does not offer VFACE, even though the VFACE panel ships with the Slicer extension. Ask whoever runs your server.

title: Heat maps are not offered by the current server setup
text: The server file for VFACE says it publishes no surface model, and the tool refuses a heat-map request without one ( VISOR:VISOR-serve server/deployment.toml:277-279 ; VISOR:SADT-VISOR tools/VFACE/src/sadt_vface/dispatch.py:452-458 ). Ask for measurements and classification. This was read in the code, not tried on a server.

title: Not yet checked on a patient
text: The VISOR version of VFACE has been tested with simulated modules, but it has not been run with the six real ones, and its results have not been compared with the legacy module's on a patient or validated clinically ( VISOR:SADT-VISOR tools/VFACE/README.md:184-193 ). Treat a verdict obtained this way as unverified.

page: VISOR: the next generation of the tools
title: Other languages
text: The French, Spanish, Italian, Korean, Portuguese and Thai versions of this site describe only the legacy code ( SlicerAutomatedDentalTools , commit 3c67957 ). They have no VISOR pages. Whatever a translated tool page says about where a computation runs, or which environment it needs, is a legacy statement. The translations will be redone later.

page: VISOR: the next generation of the tools
title: Not on this list on purpose
text: Speed, accuracy and equivalence of outputs are not compared here. The server benchmarks ( VISOR-serve benchmarks/ ) were measured before the admission engine was rewritten on 2026-09-21, and the one parity session on record found byte-identical outputs for only one tool of six. Nothing on this site claims that VISOR reproduces the legacy results bit for bit.

page: VISOR: the next generation of the tools
title: Where a Remote module differs from a pure panel
text: ALIRemote and AREGRemote send one request to a facade, and the server picks the engine (see facades ). FlexRegRemote recomputes the outline of the patch locally, about 18 ms on a 294,000-point arch, so that the joysticks respond; the real patch is computed on the server at Apply ( FlexRegRemote.py:14-18 ).

This page describes VISOR , the server generation, not the legacy Slicer code that the rest of this site documents. Citations are file:line followed by the repository: VISOR-serve at commit e9a7e5d (lines of server/main.py unless a path is given), AutomatedDentalToolsRemote (the Slicer client) at 19b95e8 , SADT-VISOR (the tools) at 6ba2a78 . The repositories carry their own documentation, and several pages of it are older than the code; where the two disagree this page follows the code and says so in a callout.…

There is no GET /benchmarks , no /benchmarks/view and no HTML page anywhere in main.py . The settings key SADT_BENCHMARK_DIR ( config.py:172 ), a block of comments about “the other two pages” ( main.py:409-420 ), an unused HTMLResponse import ( main.py:26 ) and a description of GET /benchmarks/view in CLAUDE.md:1192 are leftovers of routes that were never merged. A search of main for those routes also finds none.

The process model is the point of the design: the server never imports a tool. SchemaTool.invoke always goes through dispatch ( registry/schema_tool.py:812-822 ) and SchemaTool.run raises RuntimeError ( :840-844 ). Only the two fixtures, Example_Tool and Test_Tool , are imported in-process. The tool's interpreter, torch and VRAM therefore disappear with the process when the run ends.

After a failure the run directory is removed at once: _tracked_run writes failed and calls runs.discard in the same breath ( main.py:1636-1642 ). A watcher that had not yet read the terminal event then finds the directory gone, and its stream just ends: EventReader.read sets finished on the missing file and returns nothing ( wire/runs.py:567-578 ). The failure itself is still reported by the POST. After a success the directory survives the end of the response.

title: Defect confirmed in the code
text: main.py:2332 raises ToolExecutionError , a name that main.py never imports: the module imports dispatch and uses dispatch.ToolFailure and dispatch.RunCancelled by attribute (the only occurrence of the bare name in the file is that raise ). The branch is “detached run, and storing the result by reference failed with OSError ”. It raises a NameError instead of the intended message, so the failure report would be wrong. The branch is rare, and no test was run against it for this page.

Stale documentation about the supervisor. The supervisor has eight members: run ( runner.py:1808 ), out ( :1785 ), tmp ( :1789 ), datapath ( :1804 ), channels ( :2134 ), declareQualityControl ( :2214 ), progress ( :2235 ) and log ( :2242 ). docs/INTERNALS.md:80 says “five members, frozen”, server/README.md:652 “five members”, and server/README.md:660 calls five levels the backstop where the code says ten.

The published benchmarks were measured with it set to 1; see the benchmark section .

title: No run timeout by default, whatever docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says
text: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:48-49 promises that “a run is capped by a per-tool timeout that kills the whole process group”. By default it is not: TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 0 and the shipped deployment.toml sets no timeout_seconds . The group kill exists ( dispatch.py:713 ) but is reached only if somebody configures a timeout. A run that hangs keeps its reservation until it is cancelled. The comment next to the setting gives the reason for the default: “a cohort legitimately takes hours” ( config.py:77 ).

QUALITY_CONTROL.md is behind the code on three points. It lists “rewind to an earlier stop for flagged patients” as to build ( QUALITY_CONTROL.md:174 ); it is implemented ( main.py:1685 , runner.rewind_to ). It says the kind of a stop is “declared; not yet read by the server” ( :173 ); the server reads it and publishes option_kind . And its diagram shows rewind to=01_ALI_CBCT patients=[...] followed by “drop the memo of 01_ALI_CBCT and after” ( :130-131 ); the real route takes to and files, and drops no memo.

title: Verified in the compose file
text: Started with docker compose up and no API_TOKEN in the environment, the server runs with the token dev-token , and with no BIND_ADDR it listens on every interface. The generated token and the loopback binding come from server_ctl.py only.

title: The two ends only meet through a terminator
text: The client refuses plain HTTP and, by its own docstring, the self-signed certificate that a server presents on its own port, "including when it runs on this very machine" ( tls.py:21-26 ). A Slicer client therefore cannot talk to a bare container: it needs a terminator with a publicly signed certificate in front. Whether one stands in front of a given instance is a fact of that deployment, not of the repositories.

title: The resume path skips the extraction cap
text: The resume path unpacks the uploaded archive with file_utils.extract_zip(landed, destination) and no max_total_bytes ( VISOR-serve server/main.py:1594 ), while the comment two lines above says it "refuses zip slip, symlink members and anything over MAX_EXTRACTED_MB before a byte is written" ( :1592-1593 ). On that path only the path checks apply; the 2000 MB cap does not. Whether a declared size that lies about the real one could be exploited was not tested.

title: Limit of the gate
text: The route is protected by the same shared token as everything else. Anyone who holds it can refuse new runs for up to 300 s at a time, and again as soon as the window ends. The cap prevents a permanent lock-out, not a repeated one. This follows from the code; it was not tried on a live server.

title: The client warns the user, once per host
text: When the user saves a server that is not the local machine, the client shows a dialog that begins "Files are uploaded unmodified. This client does not de-identify anything" ( Remote .../settings_qt.py:101-132 , called from ServerToolsSettings.py:145 and SlicerCloud.py:1059 ). It is skipped for loopback and tracked per host ( settings_qt.py:73-88 ). The header comment of main.py:4-5 is therefore false for the current client; the spec and SECURITY.md:130 both say as much.

title: Absent from the three VISOR repositories
text: VISOR-serve, AutomatedDentalToolsRemote and SADT-VISOR contain no attestation, no key exchange and no application-level encryption of the files. A search for attestation , TEE , nonce , ECDH , X25519 , HPKE , enclave and key exchange in them, and in the two legacy/ trees, finds only unrelated hits (the shell command tee , a recommendation to prefer ECDHE in a TLS configuration, the DICOM "Confidentiality Profile"). Protection of data in transit is TLS alone, section 3.

title: Declared by the prototype itself
text: The header of voltcrypt/attestation.py:3-24 is a boxed warning, "simulated trust root": the signing key is a software Ed25519 key on the server's disk, which a server administrator can read to forge a false attestation. cryptoserve/enclave.py:32-43 announces "tee": "SIMULATED, aucune protection materielle" and "gpu_confidential": False , and debug: False and swap: False are constants chosen by the server, not read from hardware. title: The assumption behind the design
text: The report's central argument is that data truly de-identified on the client would take the server out of HIPAA scope. That requires a provable de-identification, which section 6 shows is not available. Until it is, the server has to be treated as one that receives patient identifiers, over a token shared by every user.
